title: mod_evasive 403s the whole site when the basemap loads tiles
description:
LIVE ON PRODUCTION as of the beeatlas-q73 deploy (2026-08-02). User-facing.

REPRODUCTION: 40 parallel HTTP range requests to /basemap/tiles/wa-20260801.pmtiles -> 40x 403. Immediately afterwards, `/` and `/data/manifest.json` ALSO return 403 for that IP. Recovers after ~10s.

CAUSE: mod_evasive is enabled (/etc/apache2/mods-available/evasive.conf) with stock thresholds:
  DOSPageCount 2 / DOSPageInterval 1     <- more than 2 hits on ONE URI per second
  DOSSiteCount 50 / DOSSiteInterval 1
  DOSBlockingPeriod 10

A PMTiles archive is a SINGLE URI that every basemap tile is read from with a range request. MapLibre issues those in parallel — a dozen or more per pan. So normal map use trips DOSPageCount permanently, and the resulting block is per-IP across the WHOLE VHOST, not just the archive: the page, the occurrence DB and the boundary GeoJSON all start 403ing. Observed in a real browser session against beeatlas.net: three 403s on the archive plus one on ecoregions-*.geojson, the latter surfacing as "Failed to load boundary GeoJSON" with county/ecoregion overlays dead for that load.

This could not happen before q73: Mapbox served tiles from api.mapbox.com, so tile traffic never reached this server. Self-hosting the basemap moved a high-rate request pattern onto the same IP+vhost as the site.

Worse than it looks: mod_evasive refreshes DOSBlockingPeriod on each request received while blocked, so a user actively panning can stay blocked well past 10s. And a shared origin (a field team on one NAT/hotspot, a school, a workshop) aggregates into one IP — exactly the situations volunteers use.

OPTIONS
 1. Tune the thresholds. DOSPageCount 2 is incompatible with range-based tiling by construction; it needs to be in the hundreds. Cheapest, keeps some protection, and needs a call on how much protection is real here.
 2. Drop mod_evasive. The read path is static files behind Apache; the module is protecting against a threat this site does not obviously have, and it is now producing false positives on normal use.
 3. Give the archive its own hostname. Does NOT work as a fix: mod_evasive counts per client IP, not per vhost.

NOT a permissions problem — the archive and the data files are 0664 with world-readable parents.

Needs an operator decision on the security posture; do not change the WAF config unilaterally.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-02, so the thresholds are not a guess.

METHOD: the real production _site bundle and a byte-identical copy of the archive (md5 verified against maderas), served from a local range-capable server — no Apache, no mod_evasive, no network. That matters: measuring against production distorts the result, because the 403s return fast and change the client's own pacing. Counts come from the browser's Resource Timing, bucketed into sliding 1s windows — the same quantity mod_evasive counts.

PEAK REQUESTS/SEC TO THE SINGLE ARCHIVE URI, one client:
   13   cold page load @ z7, 1400x900
    9   jump to z14
   12   six pans @ z14, 700ms apart
   21   zoom sweep 14->11->14
   17   cold jump to z14, 1920x1200
   31   cold zoom sweep, 1920x1200
   75   TEN PANS 120ms APART, 1920x1200   <-- worst legitimate case measured

SITE-WIDE PEAK, cold load @ z14, 1920x1200: 35/s over 36 requests (17 tiles, 5 data, 5 assets, 3 glyphs, 2 sprites, 4 other).

So DOSPageCount 2 is exceeded by a factor of ~37 during ordinary panning, and DOSSiteCount 50 is within a factor of 1.5 of a plain page load before any panning at all.

WHY THE CEILING IS NOT A CONSTANT. Requests scale with viewport area (tiles per screen) times gesture rate. 1920x1200 with 512px tiles is ~16 tiles per screen; a pan that moves a full screen re-requests about that many. A 4K display, or a faster fling, goes higher than 75. And mod_evasive counts per CLIENT IP: a field team on one hotspot, or a workshop behind one NAT, aggregates. So the right number is not "the peak we measured" — it is the peak times a headroom factor for display size and for users sharing an address.

PREFORK MAKES IT FUZZY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. maderas runs mpm_prefork and mod_evasive's hash table is per child process, so one client's requests are split across children and no child sees the whole rate. That is why the 403s are intermittent rather than constant — and why a threshold fitted tightly to a measured peak will still fire unpredictably. It argues for generous headroom, not precision.

SUGGESTED, given the above: DOSPageCount 300, DOSSiteCount 500, leaving the 1s intervals alone. That is ~4x the measured worst case for a single large client, which absorbs a bigger display and a few users on one IP, while still stopping the runaway-script case the module exists for. Lengthening the intervals instead is the wrong lever: it raises the count proportionally AND makes the block slower to clear.

Worth stating plainly: at these values mod_evasive is no longer doing much. If the answer is "we do not want a WAF on a static site", removing it is a more honest outcome than numbers chosen to never fire.

title: Vite 8.1.4 (rolldown) breaks Lit decorator transpilation — prod outage; pin vite <=8.0.16
description:
Dependabot PR #50 (npm-minor-patch group, commit f1ed5e37) bumped vite 8.0.16->8.1.4. Vite 8 uses the rolldown bundler; 8.1.4's rolldown/oxc STOPPED transpiling Lit legacy decorators. Build exits 0 but emits raw '@r(`bee-header`)class' and ';@n({attribute:!1})' into the component chunks. Browsers reject '@' => 'Uncaught SyntaxError: illegal character U+0040' in every JS file => beeatlas.net fully down 2026-07-10 ~22:35Z. Deploy 'failed' only at the Lighthouse step (NO_FCP) but S3 upload/CloudFront-invalidation already ran, so the broken build went live.

FIX SHIPPED: reverted #50 (commit 44e424af) restoring vite ^8.0.16 -> clean build (0 raw decorators), pushed, redeployed.

FOLLOW-UP: (1) pin/constrain vite so dependabot can't re-bump into 8.1.x until decorator transform is fixed — add an ignore rule in .github/dependabot.yml for vite >=8.1, OR pin exact. (2) Investigate whether rolldown-vite needs an explicit oxc decorator/transform option for 8.1+. (3) Harden deploy.yml: run a post-build assertion that no raw class/property decorators leak into _site/assets before S3 sync (grep gate), so a green build can't ship broken JS. (4) Consider making the Lighthouse NO_FCP failure gate the S3 sync (deploy AFTER audit passes) so a broken build never reaches prod.
notes: SECOND manifestation found during Group-1 runtime UAT (2026-07-11): vite 8.1/rolldown 1.1 oxc also stopped honoring tsconfig useDefineForClassFields:false. Effect: a declare-only Lit field (@query('#map') mapElement!) is emitted as a real class field that SHADOWS the decorator's prototype getter → this.mapElement undefined → new mapboxgl.Map({container:undefined}) throws → MAP NEVER RENDERS. Build passed, 977 unit tests passed (bee-map is mocked), decorator grep = 0 — ALL green; only real-browser DOM probing caught it. Fix: oxc.assumptions.setPublicClassFields + oxc.typescript.removeClassFieldsWithoutInitializer (= useDefineForClassFields:false per rolldown binding). IMPLICATION FOR #3: a raw-@ grep gate is NOT sufficient; the gate must also assert the app boots + map constructs in a real/headless browser, or at minimum grep that declared @query fields are not emitted as shadowing class fields. Live site (8.0.16) unaffected — 8.0.16 still honors tsconfig.
close_reason: All parts done. Immediate outage fix shipped+live (oxc config, vite ^8.1.4). Follow-ups: (1) dependabot pin resolved-by-obsolescence — transform is fixed AND the new boot gate catches any future vite/oxc regression before prod, so bumping vite is safe; (2) oxc decorator+useDefineForClassFields config in vite.config.ts + eleventy.config.js (commit 63a5d661); (3)+(4) commit 82209e55: scripts/smoke-boot.mjs runs in the deploy build job BEFORE artifact upload (blocks the deploy job on failure, so a broken build never reaches S3 — no Lighthouse coupling). Gate = acorn ES-module parse of every chunk (catches raw-@ MODE 1) + headless-chromium boot asserting bee-atlas/bee-map upgrade and @query mapElement resolves (WebGL-independent, catches useDefineForClassFields MODE 2). Verified: good build passes locally + in CI; disabling each oxc key reproduces the matching failure and the gate blocks it while the build still exits 0.

title: Published region layers are ~15x too coarse: maderas's geography tables need a reload
description:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND, AND IT IS NOT THE PERCENTAGE. Superseding the original writeup
below the line — that one blamed a stale 3% tuning, and the 3% is correct.

THE BUG: topology_postprocess has been re-simplifying its OWN OUTPUT.

Before beeatlas-hyq (136bce2f, "distinct outputs, no sibling-file mutation") this
step wrote its simplified result back over the raw mart IN PLACE. Those files are
still sitting in the RAW slot of every long-lived EXPORT_DIR, and the raw copy is
only refreshed when stelis decides `place-marts` needs to re-run. So each later
run feeds an already-simplified file back through -simplify, and the layer gets
quietly coarser. Nothing downstream notices: the file is present, valid, and the
right shape.

PROOF, no inference needed. `_meta` is written by exactly one function,
_inject_meta, and only ever onto this step's OUTPUT. A dbt mart out of
emit_feature_collection has none. Every raw-slot file in public/data carries one:

  public/data/ecoregions.geojson   _meta git_sha 668d53ca, built_at 2026-07-10
  public/data/counties.geojson     _meta git_sha 668d53ca, built_at 2026-07-10
  public/data/wilderness.geojson   _meta git_sha 668d53ca, built_at 2026-07-10
  data/dbt/target/sandbox/ecoregions.geojson   (no _meta — the real mart)

WHAT IT COST, measured against the live artifacts:

                    published (2026-08-01)   correct single pass    ratio
  ecoregions             761 vertices             4,674              6.1x
  counties             1,777 vertices            20,657             11.6x

Counties are the worse case, and it is not subtle. They are configured None —
no -simplify at all — so the published file is a FOSSIL of the era when they
were simplified, passed through untouched ever since:

  county      published            correct
  San Juan    24 vtx,  1 part      1,030 vtx, 22 parts
  Pierce      86 vtx,  1 part      1,494 vtx,  7 parts
  Whatcom     30 vtx,  1 part        578 vtx,  5 parts
  Island      37 vtx,  1 part        560 vtx,  3 parts

San Juan County — an archipelago — is published as ONE 24-vertex polygon. The
comment above the counties entry warns that simplification "chops small islands
like Vashon"; the warning is in the code and the damage is in the published file.

FIXED (this commit): _assert_not_our_own_output refuses to run when the input
carries _meta, naming the file, its stale sha, and the remedy. Loud, because the
failure it replaces is silent and cumulative. The step also now logs VERTICES,
not just bytes — bytes move with coordinate precision and _meta and hid a 6x
detail loss behind a plausible-looking size.

STILL TO DO — OPERATIONAL, on maderas:
  The guard will fail the next nightly, by design. Refresh the three raw slots
  from the dbt sandbox and re-run:
      cp data/dbt/target/sandbox/{counties,ecoregions,wilderness}.geojson $EXPORT_DIR/
  Expect the log to read 102,699 -> 4,674 vertices for ecoregions and
  20,657 -> 20,657 for counties. Published sizes go 38.5 KB -> ~190 KB
  (ecoregions) and 55 KB -> ~510 KB (counties); both are lazily fetched only when
  a region mode is chosen, and ~200 KB was the original budget.

  Then confirm why stelis considered `place-marts` satisfied while
  `topology-postprocess` re-ran — if the raw copy can go stale relative to the
  sandbox, the guard turns that into a failure every time rather than a fix.

---- original writeup (percentage hypothesis — WRONG, kept for the record) ----

Ecoregions are the least detailed layer on the map: 761 vertices over 64
features, 11.9 per feature, against counties' 45.6 and wilderness's 358.7. 46 of
the 64 published features have fewer than six vertices. I attributed this to a
stale 3% retention in _SIMPLIFY_PCT, on the strength of a comment budgeting
~193 KB for a file that ships at 38.5 KB. The comment is right and the shipped
file is wrong: a correct pass over the real mart lands at 192,741 bytes, matching
the comment to the byte. The 3% never drifted; the input did.

Also disproved while investigating: the WA outline used by marts/ecoregions_geo's
ST_Intersection is NOT generalized — it carries 7,945 points, and the clip takes
the EPA L3 set from 158,945 to 102,699 vertices, which is a real clip and not a
lossy one.
notes:
MADERAS DOES NOT MATCH THE DIAGNOSIS — checked from stelis 2026-08-03, before any nightly ran the new guard.

The raw slot on the SERVING host is clean and always has been. /var/www/beeatlas.net/var/export/{counties,ecoregions,wilderness}.geojson carry NO _meta, and they were rewritten Aug 3 03:07 by that night's place-marts run. So the poisoned raw slot is a fact about the local checkout's public/data, not about maderas, and data/refresh-region-marts.sh is a NO-OP there. The guard will never fire on maderas.

The published degradation on maderas is REAL but upstream of this step. Vertex counts, same dbt code both hosts:

                    maderas sandbox    local sandbox
  counties.geojson       1,305           20,657
  ecoregions.geojson     2,574          102,699

The mart itself is coarse. Cause is the geographies source. geographies.us_counties has the same 3,235 rows on both hosts, but the geometry differs ~15x: sum(length(wkt)) is 1,575,300 on maderas against 23,395,404 locally. The two schemas are not even the same shape — maderas's table carries geometry_wkt + _dlt_load_id + _dlt_id, the local one has geom alone — so the hosts loaded geographies from different sources or by different loaders.

So: maderas needs its geography RELOADED at full resolution, and the local checkout needs the raw-slot refresh. Two different fixes for one symptom.

AND THE RELOAD WILL APPEAR NOT TO WORK. Filed as stelis st-7hw: dbt-build's declared inputs in beeatlas.rkt do not name geographies.{ecoregions,us_states,us_counties,padus_wilderness}, so reloading them changes nothing the cache hashes and dbt-build will skip on the degraded marts. Fix st-7hw first, or force with a cache clear.

ANSWERING THE OPEN STELIS QUESTION at the end of the description — 'why stelis considered place-marts satisfied while topology-postprocess re-ran'. It did not. place-marts ran (raw slots Aug 3 03:07); topology-postprocess correctly did NOT (its .clean outputs are still Jul 31 20:23), because place-marts re-copied byte-identical content and the skip is on content, not mtime. That is the design working. Pre-hyq the loop was self-feeding rather than cache-driven: topology overwrote its own INPUT, so its input changed every build, so it re-ran every build and compounded — while place-marts, when it ran, laid down a clean raw for it to eat again. Stelis's part in the silence is separate and now filed: it verifies that outputs EXIST but not that they still MATCH, for every kind except db-relations (stelis st-3q7).
(correction: the stelis output-verification issue is st-zh2, not st-3q7.)
stelis st-7hw is FIXED (stelis 5245ad4). dbt-build now hashes all 22 source() tables, geographies.{us_counties,ecoregions,us_states,padus_wilderness} included — so a geography reload on maderas will invalidate dbt-build and rebuild the marts instead of cache-skipping. Do the reload after maderas pulls that stelis commit (the nightly auto-follows stelis main).
OPERATIONAL TODO IS DONE — verified end to end 2026-08-04.

The nightly of 04:49:14Z (stelis a315d58) ran green and published. Both region layers are
now correct in the export dir AND on the served root:

    counties.clean.geojson    20,657 vtx / 39 feat  -> counties-05f30bc8bbe5.geojson    511,686 B
    ecoregions.clean.geojson   4,674 vtx / 66 feat  -> ecoregions-82824060bba4.geojson  192,748 B

against 1,777 / 55,449 and 761 / 38,510 before. The ecoregions figure lands within 7 bytes
of the ~192,741 this issue predicted, and the layer is back to 66 features from 64 — the two
that simplification had erased. San Juan County is no longer a 24-vertex polygon.

Both raw slots are clean and neither carries _meta: /var/www/beeatlas.net/var/export on
maderas and public/data in the local checkout. The guard has nothing left to fire on.

Note for the record that the maderas half of the remedy in the description was never
needed — that host's raw slot was never poisoned (see the 2026-08-04 investigation note
above); its marts were coarse because geographies.us_counties itself was, which is what
the reload fixed. refresh-region-marts.sh was the right fix for the LOCAL checkout only.

Also worth knowing going forward: stelis st-zh2 now verifies output CONTENT on a skip, not
just existence. Writing into EXPORT_DIR behind stelis's back — which is exactly what
refresh-region-marts.sh does — now makes the owning task rerun and heal itself rather than
persisting silently. That is the failure mode this whole issue was about, and it is now
caught by the engine. The topology_postprocess guard is still worth keeping: it catches a
poisoned INPUT before bad output is produced, which is a different and still-uncovered case.

Remaining here is beeatlas's own call — whether the script and the guard stay as they are.
close_reason: PUBLISHED 2026-08-04T01:33Z. Live counties 1,777 -> 20,657 vertices (San Juan back to 22 parts / 1,030 vertices from a single 24-vertex blob); ecoregions 761 -> 4,674. Root cause was maderas's geography tables loaded from a coarser vintage, not the _meta feedback loop (that was the dev checkout only). Guard, vertex logging and refresh script all shipped and earned their keep. The reload needed a manual output-delete to defeat a stelis cache skip — filed as beeatlas-xwh.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text:
GUARD + REMEDY SHIPPED (64bfd090, 2af4d337). One operational step left, and it is one line.

The next nightly on maderas will FAIL this guard by design — the raw slots there
carry _meta from the pre-hyq era, same as the local ones did. Fix:

    bash data/refresh-region-marts.sh

Then re-run the pipeline. The step now logs vertices, so the confirmation is
visible in the nightly log:

    counties.geojson   -> counties.clean.geojson:   20,657 -> 20,657 vertices
    ecoregions.geojson -> ecoregions.clean.geojson: 102,699 -> 4,674 vertices

Published sizes move 55 KB -> ~510 KB (counties) and 38.5 KB -> ~190 KB
(ecoregions). Both are fetched lazily, only when a region mode is chosen, and
~200 KB was the original budget for ecoregions.

Still open after that: work out why stelis considered place-marts satisfied while
topology-postprocess re-ran. If the raw copy can drift from the sandbox at all,
the guard converts that into a nightly failure every time rather than a one-off —
which is the right failure, but it wants understanding rather than repeated
manual refreshes.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text:
CORRECTION AFTER LOOKING AT MADERAS DIRECTLY. My diagnosis was right about the
mechanism and wrong about where it applies. Two separate problems, and production
has the other one.

1. THE FEEDBACK LOOP IS REAL BUT LOCAL. Every raw-slot file carrying _meta was in
   the dev CHECKOUT's public/data. On maderas the real EXPORT_DIR is
   $BASE_DIR/var/export, and its counties.geojson / ecoregions.geojson carry NO
   _meta — they are genuine mart copies, freshly placed by place-marts at
   2026-08-03 03:07. The guard would never have fired there. It is still worth
   having (it fires on any long-lived dev tree, and the class of bug is real), but
   it was not what degraded the published layers.

   The first refresh run on maderas also went to the checkout rather than
   $BASE_DIR/var/export, because the script defaulted EXPORT_DIR to public/data.
   Fixed in 51f6d4cd: it now refuses to guess on a deployed host.

2. PRODUCTION'S COARSENESS IS THE SOURCE TABLES, AND IT IS ALREADY A KNOWN ISSUE.
   Measured on maderas's own DB (/var/www/beeatlas.net/var/beeatlas.duckdb) against
   the same tables locally:

                       maderas          local        ratio
     us_counties        69,392      1,034,082        14.9x
     ecoregions        129,170      3,316,867        25.7x

   Identical ROW counts on both (3,235 and 2,548) — same features, ~15-26x fewer
   vertices each. The cached zips on maderas are correct (us_counties.zip is
   11,626,066 bytes, byte-for-byte the current cb_2024_us_county_500k), and
   geographies_pipeline.py does not simplify. So the TABLES were loaded from an
   older, coarser vintage and never reloaded after the source URL moved from
   cb_5m to cb_500k.

   stelis already documents this, at src/beeatlas.rkt around the dbt-build task:
   "maderas's counties.geojson mart carries 1,305 vertices against 20,657 for the
   same 39 counties locally, because its geographies.us_counties.geom is ~15x
   coarser — and a reload to fix that would have changed nothing this task hashed."
   st-7hw added the five geography tables to dbt-build's input list precisely so a
   reload now invalidates it. That fix is in place; the reload has not been run.

THE REMAINING ACTION, on maderas, after the nightly finishes:

     cd ~/dev/beeatlas/data
     DB_PATH=/var/www/beeatlas.net/var/beeatlas.duckdb uv run python geographies_pipeline.py

   Then a normal nightly. dbt-build will re-run because its input address changed,
   and the region marts come out at full detail; topology_postprocess will log the
   vertex counts so it is visible.

   Expect afterwards: geographies.us_counties ~1,034,000 vertices,
   geographies.ecoregions ~3,317,000, and the WA county subset at ~20,657 rather
   than the ~1,400 it publishes today.

WHAT STAYS TRUE FROM THE ORIGINAL WRITEUP: the published artifacts really are far
too coarse (San Juan County as a single 24-vertex polygon is measured from the
live file), the vertex logging is worth having either way, and the _meta guard
stands on its own merits.

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text:
SEQUENCING WARNING for the geographies reload, learned from the failed gate.

The reload changes county and ecoregion assignment for every record near a
boundary — that is the point of it — and two integration tests compare the fresh
sandbox against the PUBLISHED parquet:

    test_occurrences_county_spatial_diff
    test_occurrences_ecoregion_spatial_diff

Both will fail on the first nightly after the reload, because the published side
was built from ~15x coarser geometry. Locally, with a fine sandbox against the
coarse published data, that is already 239 county rows and 37 ecoregion rows
flipping between adjacent in-state counties (Yakima/Pierce, Douglas/Chelan,
Kittitas/Grant). On maderas today both sides are coarse, which is why the gate has
been passing.

So the run that follows the reload needs the documented one-time bypass:

    SKIP_INTEGRATION_GATE=1 bash data/nightly.sh

and the run after that must be green again with no flag — same pattern as the
occurrences-contract release sequence. Both assertion messages now say this
inline and name this issue (2e288926), so nobody has to remember it.

ALSO FIXED THERE: test_occurrences_has_rows_and_zero_null_county_or_eco asserted
county was never NULL, which was only true because of the uncapped fallback
(beeatlas-8pz). It was pinning the bug. Replaced with rarity plus 'no null inside
the WA bbox' plus 'a null ecoregion implies a null county'.

title: Offline: no occurrence points on the map
description: Reported on device. NOT reproduced: offline in Chromium the occurrence data loads (101,516 features) and dots render — 43 dots + 309 clusters at Puget Sound, 41 + 111 at Yakima, but only 2 + 2 at Rainier z13, which is genuinely sparse. So check WHERE it was observed before assuming the layer is broken. If the data itself failed to load the loading curtain would hang instead, and it did not. /app/?diag=1 reports style layer count, which distinguishes 'no dots' from 'no style at all'.
close_reason: Same root cause as beeatlas-z30 — GeoJSON clustering runs on the MapLibre worker, which was dying offline. Device-confirmed: 31 dots + 266 clusters on screen offline.

title: Offline: hillshade renders on some tile quads and not others
description: Reported on device: offline, some quads show hillshade and some do not, and which ones changes with zoom. Online it renders normally. Most consistent with a MIX of tile sources — some terrain tiles served from the Cache Storage Blob and some attempted over the network and failing, since MapLibre marks a failed tile errored and does not retry, giving permanent holes that move as you zoom to different tiles. NOT reproduced locally: with both archives present, an offline cold start made ZERO .pmtiles network requests and rendered normally. Note queryRenderedFeatures on a hillshade layer always returns 0 (raster layers have no queryable features), so that is not a usable check — compare pixels or tile state instead. Needs /app/?diag=1 from the device: the archives section will show whether the terrain archive is present and its exact size (expect 60,813,576 bytes).
close_reason: Root cause: MapLibre's worker died offline on its sibling module import (uncontrolled SW client). Fixed by bundling the worker into one self-contained file. Device-confirmed: both sources loaded=true, hillshade renders.

title: Offline: header wraps to two lines on device
description: The header renders on two lines in the installed PWA offline. NOT reproducible in Chromium: measured 46px (single line) online AND offline at both 390px and 430px viewports, with the same DOM (h1 + 4 icon buttons, all y=0..46). So it is iOS/Safari-specific or depends on state the emulation does not have — a signed-in avatar, the Offline pill, or safe-area insets. Get /app/?diag=1 output plus a screenshot of the header from the device before guessing further.
close_reason: The Offline pill's ~70px label was outside the mobile header budget; 247+186=433 against a 430px viewport tripped the flex-wrap safety net. Label hidden below 640px, icon + aria-label carry the state.

title: UAT: map interaction sweep after the MapLibre swap
description:
A variety of map interactions were reported broken after the MapLibre swap
(beeatlas-q73), which rewrote ~870 lines of src/bee-map.ts including the entire
click path. This issue tracks the sweep and the fixes that come out of it.

SCRIPT: docs/runbooks/map-interaction-uat.md — desktop + mobile/installed PWA,
~60 checks with expected behaviour beside each. Written as a runbook rather than a
one-off checklist because the map interaction surface will need re-testing after
any future renderer change.

WHY SCRIPTED. The interaction layer is a priority chain and the failures are
order-dependent: a point on top of a county fill, a drag that ends over a dot, a
tap after a tap. Free-form clicking is exactly what misses those.

STRUCTURAL CHANGE MOST LIKELY TO HAVE CAUSED REGRESSIONS. Mapbox's addInteraction
gave five INDEPENDENT handlers whose preventDefault() stopped propagation to the
next; _clickConsumed only guarded the generic empty-click fallback. MapLibre has
no equivalent, so all five became one ordered hit-test in a single 'click'
listener that returns early on _clickConsumed. Anything depending on the old
independence, or on the exact layer order, is where to look first.

ALREADY TESTED AND RULED OUT — do not re-chase:
 - Cursor/hover feedback: there were no mouseenter/mouseleave handlers before the
   swap either. Nothing regressed; there was never anything there.
 - "Only the first tap works on touch": the single click listener returns early
   when _clickConsumed is set and only mousedown clears it, which looked certain
   to break every tap after the first. Measured with touch emulation against
   production: MapLibre fires touchstart -> mousedown -> click on EVERY tap, so
   the flag clears each time. Three consecutive taps all dispatched.
 - Click-target parity: the new 5-entry chain (clusters, unclustered-point,
   county-fill, ecoregion-fill, place-fill) matches the old five addInteraction
   handlers exactly. Nothing was dropped.

So static analysis has been exhausted; the observed breakages are the ground
truth. Capture per failure: URL, step number, expected, actual, console output

title: Cold page load ships ~37 MB uncompressed; ~10 MB is achievable
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-02 at the default WA view (z7, 1400x900), byte-counted AT THE SERVER so that worker fetches are included — the occurrence database is fetched inside a Web Worker and never appears in the page's Resource Timing, so measuring from the page silently omits the largest item by an order of magnitude.

A COLD LOAD TODAY IS 37.01 MB OVER 35 REQUESTS:

    32.24 MB   1 req   occurrences.db          (fetched in the SQLite worker)
     1.38 MB   6 req   other data artifacts
     1.29 MB   5 req   js + css bundle
     0.84 MB  13 req   basemap tiles
     0.53 MB   1 req   wa-sqlite.wasm
     0.48 MB   2 req   maplibre worker + shared
     0.22 MB   3 req   glyphs
     0.02 MB   2 req   sprites

TWO THINGS ARE SERVED WITHOUT COMPRESSION, AND BOTH ARE ONE-LINE FIXES.

1. THE DATABASE, 32.24 MB. Apache assigns `.db` NO Content-Type at all, so no
   AddOutputFilterByType rule can match it. It compresses extraordinarily well:
       gzip -1   6.39 MB   5.3x
       gzip -6   5.36 MB   6.3x
       gzip -9   5.22 MB   6.5x
       brotli -5 4.37 MB   7.7x

2. ALL JAVASCRIPT, 1.29 MB. The vhost list (infra/maderas/beeatlas.net.conf:37)
   names `application/javascript`, the legacy type. Apache serves .js and .mjs as
   `text/javascript` — see /etc/mime.types — so the filter never matches. CSS and
   JSON in the same list DO compress, which is what makes it look like
   compression is working. Confirmed against production:
       text/css          -> gzip
       application/json  -> gzip
       text/javascript   -> NOT compressed
   Note mods-available/deflate.conf DOES list text/javascript; the vhost's own
   AddOutputFilterByType replaces that list within the vhost rather than adding
   to it, which is why the global default does not save us.
   The bundle gzips 1.29 MB -> 0.32 MB (4.0x); maplibre-gl-shared.mjs 0.48 -> 0.13.

FIXING BOTH TAKES THE COLD LOAD FROM ~37 MB TO ROUGHLY 10 MB.

DO NOT JUST ADD .db TO mod_deflate. Compressing 32 MB on the fly costs real CPU
on every cold load, and maderas serves this with prefork. The data artifacts are
CONTENT-HASHED and immutable (see the LocationMatch in the vhost), so the right
shape is to pre-compress at build time — scripts/postbuild-data.mjs already owns
_site/data wholesale — and serve the .gz/.br variant with Content-Encoding via a
RewriteRule on Accept-Encoding. Zero per-request CPU, and it buys the freedom to
use maximum compression, or brotli, which the on-the-fly path could not afford.

The JS side is different: those are small enough that on-the-fly DEFLATE is fine,
and the fix is genuinely one word in infra/maderas/beeatlas.net.conf.

NOT CAUSED BY THE MAPLIBRE MIGRATION — both predate it. The migration's own
effect on cold-load weight is +0.82 MB same-origin (basemap tiles, glyphs,
sprites and the maplibre worker now come from us) against -0.74 MB of bundle,
and the old build additionally fetched from api.mapbox.com, so the true net is
smaller still. Beside a 32 MB database it is noise either way.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it is a regression rather than an omission — both gaps date to the CloudFront -> Apache move (st-jeu / st-vjd, 2026-07), and BOTH were solved before.

JAVASCRIPT was compressed by CloudFront's automatic compression. 06253107
("fix(infra): enable CloudFront compression on /data/*") set `compress: true` on
both behaviours together with enableAcceptEncodingGzip + Brotli on the custom
cache policy — it documents that `compress: true` is "silently a no-op" without
the Accept-Encoding cache-key opt-in. That went away with the distribution in
9f8e7eb0. Apache picked up CSS and JSON but not JS, because the vhost names the
legacy `application/javascript` while Apache serves `text/javascript`.

THE DATABASE was pre-compressed EXPLICITLY, for exactly the reason it is
uncompressed today. f676900e added `_upload_hashed_gz` to data/nightly.sh:

    # Like _upload_hashed but pre-compresses with gzip and sets Content-Encoding: gzip.
    # CloudFront won't auto-compress application/octet-stream, so we do it ourselves.
    # Hash is computed from the uncompressed source so content addressing is stable.
    _upload_hashed_gz() {
        local src="$1" basename="$2"; shift 2
        local ext="${src##*.}"
        local hash; hash=$(sha256sum "$src" | awk '{print $1}' | cut -c1-12)
        local hashed_name="${basename}-${hash}.${ext}"
        local gz_tmp; gz_tmp=$(mktemp)
        gzip -9 -c "$src" > "$gz_tmp"
        aws s3 cp --cache-control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" \
            --content-encoding gzip "$@" "$gz_tmp" "s3://$BUCKET/data/$hashed_name"
        rm "$gz_tmp"; echo "$hashed_name"
    }

It died with the S3 upload legs in b1d2ab4d (model-y C, "AWS serving legs
deleted"). Nothing replaced it, because merge-swap publishes files to a
filesystem rather than uploading them with metadata, and Content-Encoding stopped
being expressible at the publish step.

SO THE FIX IS RESTORING A KNOWN PATTERN, not inventing one — and the deleted code
already settles the design question this issue raised: HASH THE UNCOMPRESSED
SOURCE, ship the compressed bytes. That keeps content addressing stable and
identical to what postbuild-data.mjs computes today, so the manifest does not
change shape. The only new part is the serving half, which S3 got for free from
object metadata and Apache needs as a RewriteRule on Accept-Encoding (or
mod_negotiation) pointing at a .gz sibling.

Also worth noting: this never worked on CloudFront for a file this size ANYWAY.
CloudFront auto-compression is capped at 10 MB, which is precisely why f676900e
had to pre-compress by hand. So the 32 MB database has only ever been small on
the wire because someone did this deliberately, and it has been shipping at full
size since 2026-07.

title: Basemap: offline prime + local pmtiles reader + glyph precache
description:
Make the basemap work offline. RISKIEST PHASE.

Do NOT serve tiles through the service worker: Cache Storage has no range semantics and the SW is not on the critical path anyway (no clientsClaim, first load uncontrolled). Instead prime the archive into Cache Storage as a byte store via the existing direct cache.put pattern (prime-orchestrator.ts:112-120, which already has streaming progress UI), then read it back with Blob.slice behind a custom MapLibre protocol backed by a pmtiles Source. Keep the reader behind an interface so OPFS can replace it if the spike says so.

GLYPH COMPLETENESS (silent field-only bug class): MapLibre fetches glyph ranges LAZILY BY CODEPOINT, so a range that was never exercised in testing renders as blank boxes offline with no error. Precache all 9 glyph files (3 stacks x ranges 0-255, 256-511, 8192-8447) + 4 sprite files via the SW glob (vite.sw.config.ts globPatterns). Add a build-time test asserting every fontstack the generated style references exists on disk with exactly that range set, so a style edit fails the build instead of failing in the field.

ALSO: basemap manifest needs an offline path (mirror src/manifest.ts:51-59 Cache-Storage self-prime); version change primes new + deletes old; the offline label (bee-map.ts:101-113) changes meaning (primed = no label; unprimed = offer the download); the cache-state denominator grows by ~227 MB; map.on('load') now fires offline so recheck ready.test.ts assumptions.
acceptance_criteria: Real iOS device, installed PWA, airplane mode, cold start: basemap + occurrence dots + LABELS with icons render at z13-14 in trail country. Re-prime after a version bump replaces rather than accumulates. Feature-flaggable back to online-only basemap.

title: Spike: iOS installed-PWA storage behavior for a ~230 MB artifact
description:
REAL DEVICE ONLY — DevTools cannot answer these, and every past offline failure here was iOS-only and silent (see memory project_pwa_offline_cold_start). Blocks the offline design.

S1: does a single ~230 MB cache.put succeed in an installed PWA, and how does it behave under interruption?
S2: navigator.storage.estimate() quota INSIDE the installed app (installed apps are exempt from the 7-day ITP eviction that would otherwise delete the basemap; a plain Safari tab is not).
S3: does the installed PWA get a SEPARATE storage bucket from the Safari tab? If so a user who primes in Safari then installs re-downloads 250 MB — and the prime UI must steer install-first-then-prime. This is a UX consequence, not just a technical one.
Also measure Blob.slice read latency off a Cache Storage entry that size, since that is the proposed tile read path.

Reminder: deleting the home-screen icon does NOT clear caches; a full Settings > Safari > Website Data delete is needed between trials.
acceptance_criteria: All three answered on real hardware with numbers; a recommendation for Cache Storage vs OPFS; findings written to the offline issue and to docs/lessons-learned.md.
notes:
HARNESS DEPLOYED 2026-08-01: https://beeatlas.net/basemap/tiles/spike.html (+ spike.webmanifest so it can be installed to the Home Screen as its own app, scope /basemap/tiles/).

Deliberately NOT in the repo or the build: dropped straight into /var/www/beeatlas.net/basemap/ on maderas, which no publish path touches. Remove with: ssh maderas 'rm /var/www/beeatlas.net/basemap/spike.*'

Measures S1 (streamed 238 MB fetch then a single cache.put, with readback verification), S2 (storage.estimate quota + usage + persist()), S3 (marker written in one context and read in the other, reporting SHARED vs OWN bucket), plus Blob.slice range-read latency for the proposed tile read path. Accumulates a JSON report so partial results survive a failure.

Verified serving: 200 text/html, manifest as application/manifest+json, and no root-scoped service worker (sw.js 404s at /) so nothing intercepts the measurements — the app SW is scoped to /app/.

Awaiting real-device run.
DEVICE RUN 2026-08-01 — iPhone, iOS 18.7, Safari 26.6, installed to Home Screen.

S1 — PASSED DECISIVELY. Single cache.put of the real 238,283,859-byte archive
succeeded in 905 ms; readback byte-exact; download 7.5 s. No chunking needed, no
truncation, no quota rejection. usage_after 227.2 MB = exactly the archive, so no
hidden storage overhead.

S2 — THE QUOTA CONCERN WAS UNFOUNDED. quota 41,231,686,042 bytes (38.40 GB),
usage 0. The planning assumption (iOS might cap near 1 GB) was wrong for iOS 18.7,
where quota scales with disk. 250 MB is a rounding error. CONSEQUENCE: storage
stops being the binding constraint on scope — a future BC region, or a
higher-resolution terrain pyramid, would fit. Download time and politeness become
the limits instead. Do NOT let this reopen z13-vs-z14 as a size argument; that
choice is about the trail-network zoom floor, not bytes.

BLOB.SLICE — READ PATH IS ESSENTIALLY FREE. 50 random 16 KB reads: median 0.00 ms
(below Safari's clamped timer resolution, i.e. unmeasurable, not literally zero),
p95 1 ms, max 34 ms (first-touch page-in), 56 ms once to obtain the Blob handle.

=> DESIGN DECISION SETTLED: Cache Storage as a byte store + Blob.slice behind a
custom MapLibre protocol. OPFS IS NOT NEEDED. beeatlas-6rs can drop the OPFS
fallback and the swappable-backend seam, which was the largest open question in
the offline phase. This also confirms NOT routing tiles through the service
worker was right.

S3 — INDICATED, NOT YET PROVEN. The installed app saw no marker and reported 0
bytes used; if /app/ had ever been opened in Safari on that phone, a shared bucket
would have shown tens of MB of SW-precached assets. So a separate bucket is
strongly suggested. BUT the report contains no S3_marker_written key, because the
JSON report is per-page-load and the Safari-side write lives in a different
session — so it cannot be confirmed from this run that the marker was ever
written. HARNESS GAP, not a run error: the marker should have been recorded in
Cache Storage-visible state, not only in the in-memory log.
CONCLUSIVE RE-TEST: write the marker from the INSTALLED app, then read it in
Safari. Both halves then sit in one known state.

ALSO OPEN: persisted = false, and persist() was not exercised. Installed apps are
exempt from the 7-day ITP eviction, but persistence also governs eviction under
storage PRESSURE — worth knowing before relying on a 227 MB cache surviving.

S3 CONFIRMED 2026-08-01 — THE INSTALLED PWA HAS ITS OWN STORAGE BUCKET.

Method that settled it: wrote the marker FROM the installed app, then read in
Safari. Safari returned its own earlier marker (where="browser"), not the one the
installed app had just written to the same cache under the same key. If the bucket
were shared, the installed write would have overwritten it. Each context sees only
its own value => separate buckets. This also retroactively validates the first
run's null read: the Safari marker had in fact been written, and the installed app
genuinely could not see it. Both directions agree.

persist() — GRANTED in the installed app, DENIED in Safari. So installed storage is

navigator.storage.persist() as part of the prime flow.

applies to EVERYTHING the app caches, so a user who primes the 33 MB occurrences

title: Basemap: separate publish + serve path for the WA PMTiles artifact
description:
Design and build a publish/serve path for the ~227 MB WA PMTiles that is DELIBERATELY SEPARATE from the existing site publish pipeline, not bolted onto it. Also vendors glyphs/sprites (838 KB) into the repo under public/basemap/.

WHY SEPARATE (all verified in code, each would bite):
 - data/merge-swap.sh:44 page-tree rsync is --delete excluding only /assets and /data, so a SITE_ROOT/basemap/ dir is DELETED on the first nightly.
 - merge-swap.sh:47 age-prunes data/ files not refreshed in 30 days; a quarterly-refreshed basemap deletes itself.
 - scripts/postbuild-data.mjs rm -rf's _site/data and re-copies every artifact EVERY build (227 MB copy per nightly) and hard-errors on a missing source, breaking every dev build without the file.

The artifact has a completely different lifecycle from site data: refreshed quarterly not nightly, immutable once published, content-addressed, needs HTTP Range support, and must never be touched by a code or note publish. Decide whether that means its own directory + publish script (data/publish-basemap.sh) with merge-swap left alone, its own Apache Location/alias outside SITE_ROOT, or its own hostname. Prefer the option where the nightly CANNOT reach it by construction rather than by an exclude that a future edit can drop.

Salvage before the prototype scratchpad is deleted: the WA clip polygon (wa_only.geojson) and the extract invocation (pmtiles extract --region=<geojson> --maxzoom=14; polygon clip beats bbox by 18-26%).
design:
RECOMMENDED SHAPE (separation by construction, not by --exclude)

Serve from a directory OUTSIDE SITE_ROOT via an Apache Alias:
    Alias /basemap /var/www/beeatlas-basemap
The nightly, the code publish and the note publish all operate on SITE_ROOT, so
none of them can reach it. No --exclude to forget; merge-swap.sh is left ALONE.
Rejected: keeping it under SITE_ROOT with --exclude='/basemap' (one careless edit
to merge-swap.sh:44 silently deletes 227 MB, and the symptom is a blank basemap in
the field, not a build failure). Rejected: a separate hostname
(basemap.beeatlas.net) -- it buys lifecycle isolation we already get from the
Alias, and costs CORS on every range request
(Access-Control-Allow-Origin + Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Content-Range,
Accept-Ranges), another TLS cert and another DNS record in infra/. Same-origin is
strictly simpler; revisit only if the artifact ever moves to a CDN.

BUILD IN PLACE ON MADERAS. pmtiles extract pulls from build.protomaps.com over
range requests -- measured 8.7 s and 304 MB transferred for WA z14. So there is no
227 MB upload from a laptop: maderas builds it directly. The build script needs the
pmtiles Go CLI on maderas.

SERVING DETAILS THAT MATTER
 - DO NOT GZIP .pmtiles. Set no-gzip for the Alias (mod_deflate on a 227 MB binary
   whose tile payloads are ALREADY compressed is pure waste, and content-encoding
   on the fly breaks byte-range semantics -- which is the entire access pattern).
 - Confirm Accept-Ranges: bytes and a 206 through Apache end to end. This is the
   single load-bearing serving property; everything else degrades gracefully.
 - Content-addressed filenames (wa-<builddate>.pmtiles) +
   Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable.

PUBLISH MECHANICS
 - Never overwrite in place: a client mid-range-request against a file being
   rewritten reads corruption, and pmtiles will fail in confusing ways. Write to a
   staging name, then atomic mv.
 - basemap/manifest.json is the ONLY mutable file and is written LAST, also by
   atomic mv. It is tiny, so the swap is genuinely atomic.
 - Keep the previous version for a grace period (30 d) so a client holding a cached
   manifest is not broken mid-download; prune after.

BACKUPS: deliberately NOT backed up. The artifact is fully reproducible from the
Protomaps daily build + the committed clip polygon + the extract invocation. Adding
227 MB/quarter to the backup buckets would buy nothing. Commit the polygon and the
script; that IS the backup.

title: Vite backend integration: drop eleventy-plugin-vite, emit hashed URLs from the manifest
description:
The concrete work of beeatlas-0gx. Replace the eleventy-plugin-vite rename-and-build coupling with Vite's documented backend-integration mode.

SHAPE:
1. vite build with explicit rollupOptions.input (7 entries, already enumerable:
   src/bee-atlas.ts, src/app-entry.ts, src/entries/{bee-header,species-index,taxon-page}.ts,
   src/index.css, src/styles/places.css) and build.manifest = true, into _site/assets.
2. A _data/assets.js reads .vite/manifest.json; templates emit the hashed script/link
   URLs themselves. Verified in the spike: the manifest carries entry -> hashed file
   PLUS the css each entry pulls in, which is exactly what the templates need.
3. Eleventy becomes pure HTML generation. No HTML passes through Vite.
4. The Vite step is gated on src/ changing, so a note publish skips it entirely.

BONUS: this deletes a documented pile of coupling workarounds. eleventy.config.js
repeats envDir, optimizeDeps, server.allowedHosts and the whole oxc/decorator block
ONLY because the plugin runs Vite rooted at .11ty-vite/ and never loads vite.config.ts.

that caused the 2026-07-10 site-wide outage.

- The dev loop is the main one. npm run dev = eleventy --serve with the plugin's Vite
  middleware. Backend mode needs a separate vite dev + templates emitting /@vite/client
  and raw module URLs in dev.

  copy is load-bearing; getting it wrong silently drops /data, /feeds, /db at runtime.
- vite-plugin-preload uses transformIndexHtml to inject link rel=preload for the hashed
  .wasm; that logic moves into Eleventy (the manifest has the wasm name).
- VitePWA injectManifest must run as a post-Eleventy step. It already uses absolute
  paths and globs _site, and its globPatterns only cover app/index.html + assets/**,
  so it does not need re-running on a note change.

title: nightly.sh syncs beeatlas but not stelis — a graph change silently fails to ship
description:
HIT FOR REAL 2026-07-25 during the beeatlas-sn8 publish.

data/nightly.sh owns 'git pull' for the beeatlas repo and is documented as the single repo entry point for the nightly. But Stelis — the DATA ENGINE that OWNS the task graph — is a SEPARATE repo at $STELIS_DIR (~/dev/stelis), and nothing in the nightly updates it. scripts/fetch-data.sh only checks that src/main.rkt exists, then runs whatever is checked out.

FAILURE MODE. Ship a change that spans both repos (a new pipeline step: Python + dbt model in beeatlas, graph node in stelis) and the nightly pulls the beeatlas half ONLY. The new dbt model runs against a graph that never produced its input:

    dbt-build │ Runtime Error in model stg_dem__elevations
    dbt-build │ Catalog Error: Table with name "dem_data.elevations" does not exist
              │ because schema "dem_data" does not exist.
    ✗ dbt-build — exit 1
    — 19 ok · 3 cached · 1 failed · 13 skipped —

Fail-safe worked (dbt-build blocked its 13 dependents, no publish, live site untouched), but the diagnosis cost a full run and the error names a missing SCHEMA, which reads like a broken migration rather than 'your other repo is one commit behind'.

Recovery was: ssh maderas; cd ~/dev/stelis; git pull --ff-only; raco make src/main.rkt.

WHY THIS RECURS. It is invisible from the beeatlas side. beeatlas CI is green, 'git status' is clean, the beeatlas commit is pushed, and the stelis commit is pushed too — every check a human runs says shipped. Only the maderas checkout disagrees, and only at dbt time.

FIX OPTIONS (decide before building)
  a) nightly.sh pulls STELIS_DIR too, alongside its own git pull. Symmetric with how
     it already treats the beeatlas repo. Weigh it deliberately: it makes every
     nightly auto-adopt stelis main, widening the blast radius of a bad stelis
     commit to 'tonight's publish' with no review step.
  b) Pin the stelis SHA in beeatlas (a .stelis-version file) and have nightly.sh
     check out that SHA. Explicit, reviewable, and makes the cross-repo dependency a
     versioned fact rather than 'whatever is on the box'. More ceremony per change.
  c) Verify-only: nightly.sh fails FAST with a clear message when STELIS_DIR's HEAD
     is not the commit beeatlas expects, instead of failing deep inside dbt. Smallest
     change; still needs a human to pull.

Relates to ADR 0007 Amendment (Model Y) and the pipeline-ordering-hazard memory — same theme: an invariant that run.py held implicitly is now split across two repos.
acceptance_criteria: A cross-repo pipeline change either ships automatically or fails immediately with a message naming the stale stelis checkout — not with a Catalog Error deep inside dbt-build.
notes:
DECIDED 2026-07-26 (stelis-side analysis). Option (a), with two additions the issue did not name.

(c) IS NOT A THIRD OPTION. Failing fast when STELIS_DIR's HEAD 'is not the commit beeatlas expects' requires beeatlas to RECORD an expected SHA — that is (b)'s .stelis-version file. (c) is (b) minus the checkout step. The real choice is two-way: auto-follow, or pin.

WHY (a) OVER (b).
1. The blast-radius objection already applies to beeatlas. nightly.sh step 1 does an unreviewed 'git pull --ff-only' on beeatlas main every night — the repo holding the dbt models and loaders. Auto-adopting stelis main is not a new risk category.
2. The gates already fail safe, and did on 2026-07-25: partial-success blocked 13 dependents, the integration gate stands before the publish, the live site was untouched.
3. Content-addressing absorbs the move. A stelis pull reads as 'code-changed through rkt-imports.rkt's closure and rebuilds exactly what the edit reaches — no full rebuild, no stale skip.
4. Empirically the repos co-evolve: of 67 stelis commits touching src/, 63 touch engine files; 32 of the 36 that touch the beeatlas graph ALSO touch the engine. A pin would put ceremony on the majority of ships, and the step you would forget is the pin — the same 'remember the other repo' miss, moved earlier.

A git SUBMODULE was also considered: it implements (b)'s pin as a tracked fact with no bespoke shell. Genuinely appealing, and the right shape IF the decision ever flips to pinning. Not needed while (a) holds.

TWO ADDITIONS (a) NEEDS.
1. 'raco make src/main.rkt' after the pull. The 2026-07-25 recovery included it; a pulled-but-unbuilt stelis is a second failure mode.
2. A NAMED failure when the pull cannot happen. A dirty or diverged stelis working tree (someone debugging on maderas) makes 'git pull --ff-only' fail; that must print a message naming $STELIS_DIR, not surface later. This is how (a) satisfies the acceptance criterion, which is written in (c)'s language.

RELATED: stelis st-7wu moves the build STATE (.stelis/ — history + cache) out of the engine checkout, which is what makes updating that checkout unambiguously safe.
close_reason:
Fixed by 6080d336 (option a): nightly.sh step 1 pulls the stelis checkout alongside this repo, runs 'raco make', and fails with a message naming STELIS_DIR when the checkout is missing, dirty, or diverged. Guard paths verified against throwaway repos (absent .git -> 78; clean -> pulls and logs the SHA + subject; diverged -> exit 1 naming the path).

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-26 on maderas: both repos pulled, the updated nightly.sh ran with the synced stelis, data build completed in 379s, site render proceeded. The cross-repo change ships automatically — no Catalog Error, no manual step.

DECISION RECORD is in this issue's notes: (c) collapses into (b) since both need a recorded SHA, so the real choice was auto-follow vs pin; auto-follow won because the nightly already adopts beeatlas main unreviewed, stelis is content-addressed so a pull rebuilds only what the edit reaches, and the repos co-evolve (32 of 36 graph-touching stelis commits also touch the engine), which would put pin ceremony on most ships. A submodule remains the cleanest form of (b) if this ever needs review-per-ship.

NEW OPERATIONAL INVARIANT: maderas's stelis checkout must stay CLEAN. The nightly now hard-fails at step 1 on a dirty tree rather than silently building stale — intended, but it means debugging left uncommitted there stops the publish, loudly and by name.

FOLLOW-UP (not a blocker, filed as stelis st-7wu): the engine checkout still holds beeatlas's build state in .stelis/. Nightly pulls do not touch it — it is gitignored — but STELIS_STATE_DIR now exists to move it under $VAR_DIR beside the DuckDB and export dir it observes.

title: CI red since 2026-07-17: JS tests need data artifacts CI does not have
description:
The 'JS tests' workflow has failed on every push since b1d2ab4d (2026-07-17, model-y C), which deleted deploy.yml and created js-tests.yml. deploy.yml carried the step that pulled data artifacts from S3 into public/data/ ('aws s3 cp s3://.../data/$HASHED public/data/$local'); js-tests.yml runs bare 'npm test' with no such step and permissions: contents: read.

Two tests in the vitest suite need those artifacts and so ENOENT on a clean runner:
  - src/tests/data-species.test.ts — imports _data/species.js, which readFileSync's <dataDir>/species.json
  - src/tests/build-output.test.ts — shells out to Eleventy, which loads the same _data/species.js

Both pass on any developer machine with public/data/ populated, which is why it went unnoticed for a day: local green and CI green are different claims when tests depend on gitignored data. js-tests.yml's own header comment already states the constraint it violates ('npm run build needs the data dir ... which CI does not have') — it just assumed the vitest suite was data-free.

FIX (option 3, chosen by user 2026-07-18): move the data-dependent tests out of the default run and into the nightly on maderas, where the artifacts genuinely exist. Rejected: adding an AWS fetch step to js-tests.yml (reintroduces cloud credentials into a workflow deliberately made credential-free), and skipping the tests when public/data/ is absent (silently drops build coverage).
design: lib/build-data-dir.js already resolves EXPORT_DIR before public/data, so the same tests run unmodified on maderas against the freshly built artifacts. Mechanism: rename to *.data.test.ts, exclude that glob from the default vitest run, opt back in via an env flag, and call it from data/nightly.sh after the data build.

title: dbt occurrences mart is nondeterministic across builds
description:
The dbt 'occurrences' mart produces a different occurrences.parquet on repeated builds from identical inputs, breaking reproducibility of occurrences.db (and any hashed artifact derived from it).

Localized (ran dbt twice + generate-sqlite twice from a fixed parquet):
- occurrences.parquet: NONDETERMINISTIC across dbt runs (sha256 2c2f64a6... vs 40194a14...) — ROOT CAUSE.
- occurrence_places.parquet: DETERMINISTIC (identical hash both runs).
- generate-sqlite from a FIXED parquet: DETERMINISTIC (identical occurrences.db) — the SQLite export is clean; it faithfully propagates its input.

Conclusion: nondeterminism lives entirely in models/marts/occurrences.sql (or an int_ dependency it selects from) — classic DuckDB-parallelism row-order. occurrence_places.sql being stable is the lead: diff the two; occurrences.sql likely lacks a stable ORDER BY on its final select / the COPY-to-parquet, or needs duckdb threads pinned.

Surfaced by the Stelis determinism harness: in ~/dev/stelis, 'racket src/main.rkt --verify --from dbt-build occurrences.db' flips to DETERMINISTIC once this is fixed.
notes: Verified by the Stelis determinism harness: occurrences.db is now byte-identical across two full rebuilds (sha1 761898069fa11d21...). Closing.
close_reason: Closed
