title: An Arizona iNat record carries a Washington ecoregion
description:
Found 2026-08-03 while testing the search camera fit (beeatlas-7nx.1).

  SELECT lon, lat, record_type, observation_id FROM occurrences
   WHERE ecoregion_l3 = 'Eastern Cascades Slopes and Foothills'
     AND (lat < 44 OR lat > 50 OR lon < -125 OR lon > -116);
  -> (-111.1393280313, 33.276649554, 'specimen', 347965072)

One row, at a coordinate in ARIZONA, assigned a Washington EPA Level III ecoregion.
It stretches that ecoregion's bbox from (-121.7, 45.7)-(-120.4, 47.3) out to
(-111.1, 33.3), i.e. from the Cascades to the Sonoran Desert.

The symptom that exposed it: framing the ecoregion's 4,676 records by min/max flew
the map to Nevada at MIN_ZOOM with essentially none of the answer on screen. The
camera no longer depends on the corpus being clean (the extent trims 2% tails), so
this is not urgent for the UI — but the row is still wrong, and it is wrong in the
mart, so every consumer sees it.

Worth checking whether this is:
  - a spatial-join defect (point-in-polygon assigning a nearest/fallback region
    rather than none), which would mean OTHER out-of-state points are silently
    getting WA ecoregions and counties too; or
  - a single bad source coordinate on iNat observation 347965072, in which case the
    join is fine and the record should be excluded or corrected upstream.

The first is much more serious than the second. Start by asking how many occurrences
sit outside the state bounding box at all, and what county/ecoregion they carry:

  SELECT county, ecoregion_l3, COUNT(*) FROM occurrences
   WHERE lat NOT BETWEEN 45.5 AND 49.1 OR lon NOT BETWEEN -124.9 AND -116.9
   GROUP BY 1, 2;
design:
RESOLVED 2026-08-04. The reported symptom was already fixed; the real gap was a
missing test.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY WAS. My local public/data/occurrences.db was from Jul 26 — a week
stale. The fabricated regions it showed are the beeatlas-8pz bug, fixed by f78e0218
"stop fabricating a county for out-of-state records" on 2026-08-03. Verified against
freshly pulled published data: the Arizona record now carries county=NULL AND
ecoregion_l3=NULL, as do the two British Columbia records.

THE RECORD IS LEGITIMATE, not corrupt: iNat observation 347965072, host_inat_login
`rainhead`, a 5-specimen sample on Parkinsonia microphylla (foothill palo verde)
dated 2026-04-06. A real, correctly-geolocated Sonoran Desert observation that
entered the corpus through the WABA iNat project. Whether out-of-state records
belong in the atlas at all is a SCOPE question, not a data-quality one — not decided
here.

NO SPATIAL-JOIN DEFECT. The hypothesis worth fearing (nearest-neighbour silently
assigning WA regions to out-of-state points) is not what is happening now. Of the 17
records outside a padded WA bbox in current data, 9 carry an ecoregion and every one
of them is genuinely INSIDE it: stg_geo__ecoregions filters to WA-INTERSECTING
regions without CLIPPING them, so the full EPA polygons continue into Idaho, Oregon
and Montana. A point in Idaho really is in Columbia Mountains/Northern Rockies. The
app's ecoregions.geojson overlay IS clipped to WA, which is what makes this look
wrong at a glance.

WHAT WAS MISSING, and is now fixed (18ac8b83): 8pz capped BOTH fallbacks at
region_snap_tolerance_deg (0.2) but asserted only county.
data/dbt/tests/assert_ecoregion_snap_within_tolerance.sql is the sibling.

Verified discriminating rather than vacuous — of 41,991 distinct points carrying an
ecoregion, 377 sit outside their assigned polygon and were snapped to it, 7 are more
than 0.05 deg out, worst is 0.1344 deg, none exceed 0.2. Roughly a third of the
ceiling to spare.

STILL WORTH KNOWING: the county ceiling has less headroom than it looks, and neither
test says anything about records with NO region at all. If out-of-state records
become common, "county IS NULL" starts meaning two different things — outside
Washington, and never resolved.
close_reason: Closed

title: Route and apply search candidates in <bee-atlas>
description:
The routing half of ADR 0028. <bee-atlas> owns the index, ranks on each `search-query`,
and owns the ONE switch that applies a picked candidate.

  _onSearchQuery(e)  -> this._searchCandidates = rankCandidates(this._searchIndex, q)
  _onSearchPick(e)   -> _applySearchCandidate(candidate)

_applySearchCandidate, by kind:
  label     -> the EXISTING path, unchanged. parseCatalogSuffix +
               lookupByCatalogSuffix, selection, the filter yield, the recentre, the
               generation guard (_catalogLookupGeneration). ADR 0020 is untouched;
               this issue must not rewrite it, only move its trigger.
  taxon     -> filterState.taxonId + taxonDisplayName (buildTaxonLabel, so the chip
               matches what the pane produces)
  person    -> filterState.selectedCollectors
  place     -> filterState.selectedPlace
  county    -> filterState.selectedCounties
  ecoregion -> filterState.selectedEcoregions

COMPOSITION RULE (ADR 0028), one rule and no per-dimension special cases:
  a search REPLACES the dimension it names and LEAVES EVERY OTHER DIMENSION ALONE.
  Searching one county after another shows the second, not both. Searching 'Bombus'
  with a year and county set gives Bombus, that year, in that county.
  This is deliberately NOT the label-number yield: a selection can be hidden by a
  filter (queryListPage intersects them), a filter can only compose to zero — which
  is a legible answer, not a broken screen.

Report the resulting record count so composing to zero is said out loud rather than
shown as an empty map. _filteredRowCount already exists.

After applying: _replaceUrlState() + the same query fan-out _onFilterChanged does.
The camera fit is beeatlas-7nx.1 and lands on top of this.

Building the index: taxa/counties/ecoregions/collectors are already @state fields
here; places arrive with the hoist issue. Rebuild the index when its inputs change —
it does not exist until the DB loads, which is why <bee-atlas> computes candidates
rather than pushing a raw index down to the header (a future kind, notes over
api.beeatlas.net, is genuinely async and must be able to arrive late).

Tests extend src/tests/bee-atlas-search.test.ts, whose existing cases (selection,
recentring, the filter yield, the stale guard, miss-vs-error) must still pass — none
of that is what is changing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Convert the search popover to a combobox (<bee-header>)
description:
ADR 0028: names resolve as you type, numbers stay submit-only. <bee-header> stays a
pure presenter — it renders candidates it is given and emits picks.

SEAM CHANGE
  out: `search-submit {query}`  (nothing left for it to carry)
  in:  `search-query {query}`   emitted on input — no debounce, matching is in-memory
       `search-pick {candidate}` emitted on choice
  props: `searchCandidates: SearchCandidate[]`, `searchCandidatesTruncated: boolean`
  `searchStatus` STAYS, all three members, with its existing rule of rendering only
  while the field still holds the same string. A numeric query's row is speculative,
  so miss/error are still discovered on pick, not on keystroke.

  Enter with nothing highlighted picks the FIRST candidate — that is what the old
  submit meant. The submit button does the same; ADR 0021 already decided to keep it
  regardless of the keypad ("on touch a visible tap target beats a keyboard
  convention").

DROP inputmode="numeric" — ADR 0021 predicted exactly this ("it will, when search
grows to names"). Also revisit the placeholder and the aria-label, both of which say
"label number" today.

BUTTONS IN A DIALOG, NOT A LISTBOX (ADR 0028). The popover is already role="dialog"
and already holds buttons. A row is a <button> plus, where href is non-null, an <a>.
An ARIA listbox option cannot contain a focusable child, so listbox semantics would
force the page link into a keyboard modifier nothing announces. Arrow keys move focus
between rows by roving tabindex; Tab reaches the link; Enter on the button applies.

ONE ROW IS ONE THING, with one primary verb (filter) and an escape hatch that leaves
the app. Group by kind with headings — kind explains a row, it does not order it.
Show the weight (record count) on the row, and say so when the list was truncated.

The two-stage Escape from ADR 0021 stands: Escape in a non-empty field clears it,
Escape in an empty field closes the popover. A pick closes the popover and empties the
field, same reasoning as the hit rule — the answer appears behind it.

Tests move/extend from src/tests/bee-header-search.test.ts.
close_reason: Closed

title: Hoist places.json from <bee-pane> to <bee-atlas>
description:
<bee-pane> fetches places.json itself (_ensurePlaceNamesLoaded, bee-pane.ts:911) and
keeps _placeNameBySlug + _placeOptions as private state. That violates the state
ownership invariant on its own terms — every other option list (taxa, counties,
ecoregions, collectors) is owned by <bee-atlas> and passed down as a property — and
search needs the same data, so a second fetch would otherwise appear.

Move the fetch to <bee-atlas> beside _loadCollectorOptions / _loadCountyEcoregionOptions,
pass `placeOptions` and the slug->name map down to <bee-pane> as properties, and feed
the search index from the same load.

Keep the two behaviours the pane already has:
  - options are filtered to places with (specimen_count > 0 OR sample_count > 0);
    the NAME map keeps every place, because a chip must still resolve a slug the URL
    carries even when that place has no records.
  - a failed fetch is swallowed and the chip falls back to the slug. Do not turn a
    missing places.json into a thrown error on the boot path.

This is a prerequisite for the search index (places are the one corpus not already in
<bee-atlas>) and stands on its own as an invariant fix.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pure search index + ranking (src/search.ts)
description:
The pure half of ADR 0028: a SearchIndex built from what <bee-atlas> already holds,
and a ranking function over it. No DOM, no SQL, no Lit — testable standalone, which
is the whole reason it is its own module.

CANDIDATES ARE DECLARATIVE DATA, NEVER CLOSURES (ADR 0028). A discriminated union
over kind plus the payload that identifies the thing; <bee-atlas> owns the one switch
that applies it. The header must not carry behaviour across the property boundary.

  type SearchKind = 'label' | 'taxon' | 'person' | 'place' | 'county' | 'ecoregion'
  interface SearchCandidateBase {
    key: string      // stable id for keyed rendering + tests, e.g. 'taxon:12345'
    label: string    // the row's primary text
    detail: string | null   // secondary text (land owner, iNat login, rank)
    weight: number   // record count — the tie-break, and shown on the row
    href: string | null     // the thing's page, when one exists; null = no link
  }
  ...plus per-kind payload: {kind:'label', suffix} | {kind:'taxon', taxonId} |
     {kind:'person', collector: CollectorEntry} | {kind:'place', slug} |
     {kind:'county', name} | {kind:'ecoregion', name}

RANKING (ADR 0028)
  1. Syntax first: parseCatalogSuffix(query) non-null => return EXACTLY ONE label
     candidate and nothing else. Digits cannot mean anything but a label number.
  2. Otherwise score: exact 3; prefix of the whole name OR of any word within it 2
     (so 'vosnesenskii' finds Bombus vosnesenskii and 'smith' finds 'Smith, J.');
     substring 1; no match drops.
  3. Ties break by weight descending — the record count behind the thing.
  4. Then by label ascending, so the list is deterministic.
  Kind is NOT a ranking key. It is a group heading. A well-attested collector must be
  able to outrank a one-record subgenus.

  Cap the list (~10) and RETURN THE FACT THAT IT WAS CAPPED, so the popover can say
  so. A silent top-N presented as the whole answer is the failure mode.

  Normalize both sides: lowercase, fold diacritics, collapse whitespace.

INDEX SOURCES — all already in <bee-atlas> except places (see the hoist issue):
  taxa        _taxaOptions (TaxonOption: label, taxonId, rank), weight = occurrence
              count per taxon; href from src/taxon-pages.ts (taxon_id -> /species/…),
              which is ABSENT for ~20 of 646 taxa and for families — null, not guessed.
  people      _collectorOptions (CollectorEntry), weight = row count;
              href = /collectors/{login}/ ONLY when host_inat_login is non-null.
  places      places.json, weight = specimen_count + sample_count;
              href = /places/{slug}.html. EXCLUDE places with zero of both — bee-pane
              already does (bee-pane.ts:922) and a filter that can only ever produce
              an empty map punishes being picked.
  county      _countyOptions — NO page exists, href null.
  ecoregion   _ecoregionOptions — NO page exists, href null.

TESTS
Pure module, so cover it properly: the digits-exclusivity rule, word-prefix matching,
weight tie-breaks, determinism on equal weight, diacritic folding, the cap flag, and
that a taxon with no page yields href null rather than a string-munged URL.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fit the map to a search result's extent (<bee-map> fitBounds)
description:
ADR 0028 decides that search moves the camera to what it just applied, while the
filter panel never does. `_viewState` cannot carry that: it is {lon, lat, zoom} and
bee-map jumpTo's it (bee-map.ts:431), but turning an extent into a camera depends on
the map's pixel dimensions, which only <bee-map> knows. So the extent has to cross
the boundary as an extent.

THE PATH
  1. <bee-header> emits `search-pick {candidate}`.
  2. bee-atlas `_onSearchPick` applies the candidate to `_filterState`, calls
     `_replaceUrlState()`, fans out the same four queries `_onFilterChanged` does.
  3. `_runFilterQuery()` (bee-atlas.ts:906) -> `queryVisibleGeoJSON` (filter.ts:665),
     behind `this._filterGuard` (makeStaleGuard, stale-guard.ts:7).
  4. THE EXTENT EXISTS HERE AND NOWHERE EARLIER: `guarded.result.geojson.features`
     is every matching point, already materialized (filter.ts:692). min/max over
     `feature.geometry.coordinates` is the bbox — no extra query, no second worker
     round-trip.
  5. bee-atlas sets the camera-command property -> <bee-map>.updated() calls
     `map.fitBounds(bbox, {padding, maxZoom})`.
  6. moveend (bee-map.ts:614) -> `view-moved` -> `_onViewMoved` sets `_currentView`
     (bee-atlas.ts:1671). The URL catches up through the existing channel; no new
     plumbing on the return path.

REPLACE `panTo`, DO NOT ADD ALONGSIDE IT
<bee-map> declares `panTo` (bee-map.ts:131) and implements a flyTo for it (:439), but
NOTHING in the tree sets it — the only reference outside bee-map.ts is
bee-atlas.test.ts:67 asserting the property exists. Row-pan goes through `_viewState`
instead (`_onRowPan`, bee-atlas.ts:1960). Adding fitBounds beside it leaves bee-map
with three camera channels, one a decoy. The ARCH-02 property test moves with it.

FOUR HAZARDS
 H1. `_runFilterQuery` has ~14 callers (774, 1036, 1552, 1660, 1766, 1826, 1850,
     1873, 1895, 1948, 2070, 2097, 2121, 2158) — every filter control, the bounds
     gesture, popstate, boot. Fitting inside the query would fly the map on every
     filter-panel change, which is exactly what ADR 0028 forbids. The fit must be a
     ONE-SHOT INTENT attached to this filter change.
 H2. That intent must be CAPTURED PER-CALL, not read at commit. `_filterGuard`
     returns null when superseded and `_runFilterQuery` returns early at :908, so a
     `_pendingFit` field read at commit time survives a superseded query and fires on
     somebody else's filter change. Capture into a local and clear the field at the
     top — the `myGen` discipline `_onSearchSubmit` already uses (:1723).
 H3. Zero features => explicit no-op (ADR 0028: a zero-match search leaves the
     viewport alone). One feature => zero-area bbox; needs a maxZoom cap or MapLibre
     slams to street level. `CATALOG_LOOKUP_ZOOM` is the existing precedent.
 H4. The fit WILL PUSH A HISTORY ENTRY. `_replaceUrlState()` sets
     `_viewportSessionActive = false` (:1298), so the following moveend reaches
     `_writeViewportHistory` with no active session and takes the pushState branch
     (:1312). Not obviously wrong — it makes a search undoable by Back, which the
     ADR 0020 filter yield never managed — but it is timing-dependent. Decide it
     deliberately and pin it with a test rather than letting it emerge.

NOTE ON WHAT GETS FRAMED
`queryVisibleGeoJSON` drops null coordinates but keeps checklist rows unless bounds
or place is set (filter.ts:530). A taxon attested only by checklist records therefore
fits to county-placeholder points. That is honest — the camera frames the dots the
reader is about to see — but it should be a conscious choice, not a surprise.
close_reason: Closed

title: stelis: dbt-build cache-skips despite a changed geography relation (st-7hw not closed)
description:
Reproduced on maderas 2026-08-03 while publishing the region-geometry fix
(beeatlas-0yv). A reload of geographies.us_counties and geographies.ecoregions —
~15x and ~26x more vertices, same row counts — did NOT invalidate dbt-build. Two
consecutive nightlies reported:

    ≡ dbt-build — cached (inputs unchanged)

and left the degraded marts in place. That is precisely the failure st-7hw set out
to close by naming the five geography tables in dbt-build's #:inputs, and the
comment in beeatlas.rkt still describes it as closed.

WHY IT IS NOT. `--why counties.geojson` answers:

    dbt-build — inputs not content-addressable: anti-entropy-applied,
      checklist-resolution-verified, corrections-verified, inactive-verified,
      inat-obs-count-verified, resolution-verified

Six 'token inputs are unaddressable, and the task then appears to fall back to a
decision that does not consult the ADDRESSABLE inputs either. Corroborating:

    --history geographies_us_counties
    → "geographies_us_counties — no observations in the history."

The relation has never been hashed in a real build. Naming it in #:inputs put it
in the dependency ORDER but never in the ADDRESS, so a content change to it is
invisible. The digest machinery itself is fine — to_json() over a DuckDB GEOMETRY
column emits full WKT, so relation-digest would see the change if it were asked.

WORKAROUND USED, for the record: delete the task's outputs. `rm
data/dbt/target/sandbox/{counties,ecoregions}.geojson` flipped it to

    ▶ dbt-build — outputs missing: .../counties.geojson, .../ecoregions.geojson

and the rebuild published correctly (counties 20,657 vertices, ecoregions
102,699 -> 4,674). So the outputs-present branch is reachable and correct; it is
the inputs-unchanged branch that is answering without looking.

WHAT TO DECIDE
 - Should a task with ANY unaddressable input be content-skippable at all? If the
   answer is no, these six tokens make dbt-build permanently unskippable, which is
   expensive but honest. If the answer is yes, the addressable inputs must still
   enter the address, or naming them is decoration.
 - Either way, an artifact that is named as an input and has NO observations after
   a real build is a detectable inconsistency. That would have caught this the day
   st-7hw shipped, instead of a month later via a 15x-coarse county layer.
 - `--why` already reports the unaddressable inputs. It does not say what it then
   DID about them, which is the sentence that would have made this obvious.

Filed from beeatlas because that is where it was found; the fix is in stelis.
notes:
INVESTIGATED FROM STELIS 2026-08-04. The cache-skip is real; both halves of the diagnosis are not.

1. WHY IT SKIPPED: maderas is running stelis d83218f, which PREDATES the st-7hw fix.
The fix is 5245ad4 in the local stelis checkout and was never pushed (stelis's standing
rule is that the user drives pushes). On d83218f, dbt-build's #:inputs name
geographies_places and nothing else from that schema — verified on the host:

    sed -n '/make-task .dbt-build/,/#:invoke/p' src/beeatlas.rkt | grep geographies
    ->  taxon_lineage_extended host_plant_lineage geographies_places

So the reloaded us_counties and ecoregions were genuinely not in the address, and the
two nightlies behaved exactly as st-7hw described. st-7hw is not reopened; it is
unshipped. The beeatlas.rkt comment that reads as closed is in the local working tree,
which is the same checkout you read — maderas's copy has neither the comment nor the
fix. Push, let the nightly's step-1 sync take it, and the reload will invalidate.

2. THE SIX-TOKEN --why OUTPUT WAS AN ENVIRONMENT ARTIFACT, not the nightly's decision.
Run on maderas back to back, same second, same graph:

  STELIS_STATE_DIR=/var/www/beeatlas.net/var/stelis   (the nightly's)
    dbt-build — inputs unchanged, but stale through upstreams

  STELIS_STATE_DIR=/tmp/empty-stelis-state
    dbt-build — inputs not content-addressable: anti-entropy-applied,
      checklist-resolution-verified, corrections-verified, inactive-verified,
      inat-obs-count-verified, resolution-verified

The second is your line, exactly. With no cache entries no gate has a recorded input
address, so every gate TOKEN is unaddressable (st-ysf) — and those six names are just
dbt-build's six token inputs. --why also needs BEEATLAS_DIR (fetch-data.sh sets it;
an interactive run does not) or it reports the AUTHOR'S laptop paths as missing code.

3. SO THE FEARED BEHAVIOUR DOES NOT EXIST. cache.rkt:307: if ANY input is unresolvable,
input-snapshot returns a 'run' decision — an unaddressed input forces a run and can
never launder into a skip. 'Unaddressable' and 'cached' cannot both be true of one
decision; they were two different states being compared.

4. --history geographies_us_counties reporting no observations is expected rather than
a symptom: observations record what tasks PRODUCE, and that relation is producerless.
Your underlying instinct is right though, and the checkable form is 'a declared input
that never appears in its consumer's recorded input-hashes' — noted on stelis st-5rl.

5. YOUR THIRD BULLET IS A REAL STELIS BUG and is now stelis st-5rl: --why reports the
unaddressable inputs without saying that this forces a run, and neither --why nor
--explain names the state dir it is answering out of. Those two together are what made
a mis-set env read as an engine bug.

The workaround you used (rm the outputs -> 'outputs missing' -> rebuild) was correct
and is the right lever until the fix ships.
CONFIRMED FIXED by the nightly of 2026-08-04T04:49:14Z (stelis a315d58), which ran green end to end and published.

    25. ▶ dbt-build
         inputs changed: checklist_raw, geographies_ecoregions,
           geographies_padus_wilderness, geographies_us_counties, geographies_us_states

The geography is in the input address and named. dbt-build ran (PASS=140 WARN=3 ERROR=0),
the integration gate passed, and the corrected layers are served: counties 20,657 vertices
at 511,686 bytes (was 1,777 / 55,449), ecoregions 4,674 at 192,748 (was 761 / 38,510) —
matching the byte estimate in beeatlas-0yv. No rm-the-outputs workaround needed.

The other two stelis fixes are visible in the same log. st-5rl: the plan now records what
it judged against —

    Reading build state: /var/www/beeatlas.net/var/stelis/cache (40 task entries)
    Resolving outputs in: /var/www/beeatlas.net/var/export

so a future reader of this log can tell whether a surprising verdict is about the build or
about the invocation. st-zh2 (outputs verified by content on a skip, not just existence):
zero output-stale across all 40 tasks in a real build — no false positives.

Closing: the engine bug hypothesised here did not exist, the reporting defect that made it
look real is fixed, and the underlying wrong-skip is fixed and verified in production.
close_reason: Resolved in stelis a315d58 (st-7hw + st-5rl + st-zh2), verified by a green published nightly 2026-08-04T04:49Z. dbt-build now names the geography in its input address; the corrected county/ecoregion layers are live.

title: Carry counties for OR, ID, NM, OK and BC regional districts, not just WA
description:
Data-side only. Today `county` is Washington-or-nothing: stg_geo__us_counties
filters `state_fips = '53'`, so a record outside WA has no county at all — since
beeatlas-8pz it is honestly NULL rather than snapped to the nearest WA county from
168 km away, but it is still county-less.

THE GEOMETRY IS ALREADY THERE, for the US at least. Nothing needs fetching:

  geographies.us_counties   3,235 counties across 56 state/territory FIPS
                            (Census cb_2024_us_county_500k — already national)
  geographies.ecoregions    2,548 polygons, lon -179.1..-52.7, lat 14.5..83.1
                            (CEC NA_CEC_Eco_Level3 — already continental North
                            America, and stg_geo__ecoregions does not clip it, which
                            is why an Idaho point already resolves correctly to
                            Columbia Mountains/Northern Rockies)
  geographies.ca_provinces  StatCan lpr_000b21a — provinces only, no subdivisions

So for OR/ID/NM/OK this is widening one WHERE clause:

  ID 44   NM 33   OK 77   OR 36   (WA 39)   = 229 counties

BC IS THE ONE THAT NEEDS A SOURCE. The BC equivalent of a county is a REGIONAL
DISTRICT, and in StatCan's vocabulary BC's regional districts ARE its census
divisions — so the layer wanted is the 2021 census-division cartographic boundary
file, sibling of the province file already loaded:

  https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2021/geo/sip-pis/boundary-limites/files-fichiers/lcd_000b21a_e.zip

(verified reachable, 200). `lcd_000a21a_e` is the higher-resolution cut of the
same thing if 000b proves too coarse. Note two mismatches to decide on, not just
plumb: a regional district is not administratively a county (it is a federation of
municipalities and unincorporated areas), and a handful of BC territory sits
outside any regional district.

THE ACTUAL WORK IS THE NAME COLLISION, not the geometry.

`county` is a bare name string — in the mart contract, in the `counties=` URL
param, in `county IN (...)` in src/filter.ts, in the checklist arm's county-range
join, and in the coverage maps. County names collide hard across exactly the five
states named:

  Lincoln     ID, NM, OK, OR, WA   (all five)
  Grant       NM, OK, OR, WA
  Jefferson   ID, OK, OR, WA
  Washington  ID, OK, OR
  ... 14 more pairs: Adams, Benton, Blaine, Clark, Columbia, Curry, Custer,
      Douglas, Franklin, Garfield, Jackson, Lewis, San Juan, Union

44 of the 229 county rows carry a name that is ambiguous within the five states.

WORSE THAN AMBIGUOUS — SILENTLY WRONG FOR EXISTING LINKS. `?counties=Grant` is a
URL shape in the wild today and unambiguously means Grant County, WA. The moment
NM/OK/OR counties land it matches four counties, and every previously-shared link
changes meaning without erroring. Eleven of the eighteen collisions are with WA
counties that can already appear in a saved URL: Grant, Jefferson, Adams, Benton,
Clark, Columbia, Douglas, Franklin, Garfield, Lewis, San Juan.

SO THE DECISION THIS ISSUE IS REALLY ABOUT: what identifies a county once there is
more than one state. Options, roughly in order of increasing honesty and cost —

 1. Qualified string, `Grant, WA`. Cheapest; keeps one column; needs a URL
    migration that reads a bare name as WA for backwards compatibility.
 2. Separate `county` + `state` columns. Cleanest to query and aggregate; two more
    columns on a contracted mart and every consumer touched.
 3. FIPS/SGC code as the key with the name as a display attribute. The correct
    answer for a system that will also carry BC (where "state" is a province and
    the code space is different), and the most work.

Whatever wins has to answer the same question for the CHECKLIST arm, which is
county-range assertions from a Washington-specific publication (Bartholomew et al.
2024) and has no out-of-state analogue — so its counties stay WA and must not
silently join to a same-named county elsewhere.

RELATED, and probably the real motivation: beeatlas-bcg (multi-state expansion) and
the memory `project_multi_state_expansion` already say geographic scope should be
configurable rather than hardcoded. This is the same decision arriving from the
data side, and the state list belongs in config next to state_fips rather than in a
literal.

ALSO: doing this retires the last of beeatlas-8pz. Those 16 out-of-state records
would get their real counties — Baker County OR for WSDA_2336960, Bonner County ID
for the Pend Oreille cluster, Maricopa County AZ for the one in Arizona (which is
not on this list, so it stays NULL and stays worth a look).

comments.author: Peter Abrahamsen
comments.text:
URL SCHEME DECIDED (2026-08-03): qualified as `WA_Grant` — state/province prefix, underscore, county name. So `?counties=WA_Grant,OR_Lincoln`.

Explicitly NOT a concern: existing bare-name URLs in the wild. No back-compat
shim, no dual parse. That removes the main cost of option 1 in the description
above and makes it the choice.

Consequences worth writing down while it is fresh:
 - The prefix is a JURISDICTION, not a US state — BC regional districts get
   `BC_` on the same shape, which is the whole reason a prefixed string beats a
   separate `state` column here.
 - It survives a bare-name collision by construction, so the 44-of-229 ambiguity
   stops being a correctness problem and becomes a display one: the UI still shows
   'Grant', with the qualifier surfaced only where two are on screen at once.
 - The checklist arm keeps WA-only counties and now cannot silently join to a
   same-named county elsewhere, because the keys no longer match by accident.
 - One migration to write: every existing `counties=` value gains a `WA_`
   prefix, and the county autocomplete, the CSV filename builder and the
   place/coverage pages all key on the new form.

title: Both offline-uat regression guards are permanently red
description:
Found in the beeatlas-ecn map-interaction sweep, section G. Neither command in
docs/runbooks/map-interaction-uat.md §G can currently signal a regression,
because both already fail on a clean tree.

1. node scripts/offline-uat.mjs --browser=chromium --prime  ->  8/9

     FAIL  no network attempts for .pmtiles
           https://beeatlas.net/basemap/tiles/wa-20260801.pmtiles,
           https://beeatlas.net/basemap/tiles/wa-terrain-20260802.pmtiles

   That is exactly beeatlas-c8v, which was CLOSED as accepted: the requests come
   from pmtiles' own FetchSource before registerPrimedArchives replaces the
   entry, they self-correct, and the tile read path is entirely local. The
   decision was to live with them. But the assertion was left asserting, so the
   run is red forever and the next person reads '8/9, same as last time' and
   stops looking. A guard nobody trusts is not a guard.

   Fix: make the check match the accepted behaviour — assert no .pmtiles requests
   AFTER the initial style application (the c8v note already establishes that
   panning four locations produced zero), and name c8v in the message so the
   startup burst reads as known rather than as a finding.

2. node scripts/offline-uat.mjs --browser=webkit  ->  uncaught exception

     page.goto: WebKit encountered an internal error

   The runbook documents this invocation as 'the Safari-engine ONLINE half', and
   the script's own header says the offline half needs chromium because
   setOffline is unreliable in WebKit. But nothing in the script acts on that:
   BROWSER is read at line 50 and the offline half at line 167 runs regardless.
   So the documented command always dies mid-run with a stack trace and a
   non-zero exit, after its two online checks have passed.

   Fix: skip the offline half when BROWSER !== 'chromium', print why, and exit on
   the online result alone.

Both are small. The point of doing them is that section G exists to catch the
next renderer change, and right now it cannot.
close_reason: Both guards now green and both now able to fail: chromium 9/9 (asserts zero .pmtiles requests while panning four locations, replacing an assertion on behaviour we had accepted), webkit 2/2 with the offline half skipped explicitly instead of crashing. Runbook §G updated.

title: Identity should survive going offline, not collapse to signed-out
description:
Raised 2026-08-03 while cutting the doomed network requests an offline cold start
makes.

fetchWhoami() cannot distinguish "signed out" from "could not ask": every network
failure resolves to {authenticated:false}, and beeatlas-6rs added an explicit
offline short-circuit that reaches the same answer without the request (and
without iOS's "Turn On Wi-Fi" modal). Behaviour is unchanged from before — but the
MODEL is wrong, and it is wrong in a way that forecloses things we want.

THE POINT, in the user's framing: if you were logged in when the data loaded, then
features sensitive to who you are should work the same way offline. None exist
yet, but "my specimens" is the natural one — and it cannot be built on a client
that discards identity the moment signal drops. The occurrence data is already
local and complete; the only missing ingredient is knowing who you are.

WHAT THIS PROBABLY LOOKS LIKE
- Persist the last successful whoami (login, role, isAuthor, iconUrl) and serve it
  when the network cannot be reached, instead of returning {authenticated:false}.
- Distinguish the three states the UI actually has: signed out, signed in
  (verified this session), and signed in (last known, unverified). Today the
  first and third are the same state, which is why an offline start shows a Sign
  in button to someone who is signed in.
- Clear it on explicit sign-out, including a sign-out that happens while offline.

CONSTRAINT, and it is the important one: cached identity is for DISPLAY and for
LOCAL FILTERING only. Authorization stays server-side and re-checked per request
— see the existing note in auth-client.ts on the curator signal being a UX
affordance, never client-trusted. Writes need the API anyway, so nothing about
this grants offline write capability.

ALREADY DONE, so it is not part of this: <bee-atlas> now re-runs fetchWhoami on
the 'online' event. Before that, a session that started offline showed a Sign in
button for the rest of its life even once back on WiFi — the field flow exactly.
That makes the current degradation temporary rather than sticky, which is what
makes deferring this reasonable.
close_reason: Shipped in 79f96c30. AuthState.verified + last-known identity replay + durable offline sign-out; ADR 0027.

title: Basemap: stray FetchSource requests at offline startup
description:
Found while verifying beeatlas-6rs offline with scripts/offline-uat.mjs.

An offline cold start with both archives primed makes 2-3 FAILED network requests
at startup, then zero thereafter:

  https://.../wa-20260801.pmtiles          (x2)
  https://.../wa-terrain-20260802.pmtiles  (x1)

A stack trace shows they come from pmtiles' own FetchSource, i.e. Protocol
created a network-backed PMTiles for those URLs before registerPrimedArchives
replaced the entry. It self-corrects: panning across four locations produced ZERO
further requests, both sources report loaded, and 85 layers render. So the tile
read path is entirely local and the map is fully usable offline.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: on iOS a failed request in a Home Screen PWA raises the
system "Turn On Wi-Fi to Use the Internet" alert. So these cost nothing
technically but are user-visible noise in exactly the situation the offline work
exists for.

NOT YET EXPLAINED. registerPrimedArchives is awaited BEFORE setStyle precisely so
this cannot happen, and the keys match (basemapArchiveUrl is the single
definition, asserted against the built style in basemap-cache.test.ts). So either
MapLibre resolves the source before the style is applied, or something applies a
style earlier than _applyBasemap. Read it, do not guess.

RELATED, probably the same root: loadBasemapManifest is called twice on boot and
is NOT memoized (unlike loadManifest in src/manifest.ts, which caches its
promise) — once by bee-map._resolveBasemapStyle and once by
bee-atlas._refreshBasemapState. Offline that is two failed manifest fetches, and
two more of those iOS alerts. Memoizing it the way manifest.ts does is likely
worth doing regardless.

REPRODUCE:
  node scripts/offline-uat.mjs --browser=chromium --fresh --prime
notes:
CORRECTION, same session: /app/sw.js DOES reach the server.

  10:33:04  200  /app/sw.js              <- launch
  10:33:11  200  /basemap/tiles/manifest.json
  10:33:11  200  /data/manifest.json
  10:33:11  200  /data/manifest.json     <- +7s, the deferred revalidations

The earlier note said sw.js was absent and inferred the nag was probably an iOS
connectivity probe outside our control. That was wrong — it was absent only from
the first filtered slice. The browser's soft service-worker update check fires at
launch, every launch, and offline it is a failed request. CAUSE CONFIRMED.

THE MITIGATION, and its cost:
  register with updateViaCache:'all' AND serve /app/sw.js with a Cache-Control
  max-age. The browser may then satisfy the update check from the HTTP cache
  instead of the network, so an offline launch within that window makes no
  request at all. The spec caps the useful window at 24h regardless of max-age.

  Cost: app updates are discovered up to max-age later, which directly weakens
  the 'App update available — tap to reload' flow. A 1h max-age barely helps the
  field case (offline all day exceeds it); 24h helps but delays updates a day.

  Also needs an Apache change on maderas — /app/sw.js currently inherits the page
  tree's max-age=0, and the vhost is not in this repo.

Decision deferred to the owner; 'do nothing' remains defensible now that the
cause is known and the map works completely offline.
close_reason: Accepted: app makes zero failed offline requests; residual OS nag is the browser's own SW update check, not app-controlled. Mitigation rejected as not worth weakening update discovery.

title: Cleaning becomes explicit and unconditional; builtAt honors SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
description:
Precondition for stelis st-hdm (the render returns to the Stelis graph as app-bundle + site-content nodes). Nothing here needs Stelis; it is worth doing on its own.

TWO CHANGES.

1. THE CLEANING STOPS BEING A SIDE EFFECT OF vite build. Today emptyOutDir:true makes the app bundle the site's cleaning boundary (ADR 0016), which is why build-app.mjs's SKIP path has to impersonate it (ADR 0019: 'a skip still cleans, removing everything except assets/'). Two code paths that must stay byte-indistinguishable, verified by comparing trees. Collapse them: emptyOutDir:false, and build-app.mjs cleans unconditionally, runs Vite only when the fingerprint moved, and prunes unnamed assets on BOTH paths. One path, no impersonation.

This is also what lets a graph node own the extent later: a producer that empties the whole of _site is writing outside its declared subtree, which one-producer-per-artifact forbids.

2. builtAt HONORS SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. _data/build.js stamps wall-clock into _scaffold-check/index.html, which ADR 0017 measured as literally the only file that differs between any two builds. Under a tree digest of the page tree that means the artifact can NEVER cut off. Matches data/feeds.py and data/topology_postprocess.py, which honor it for exactly this reason, and extends ADR 0019's own rule ('nothing clock- or HEAD-derived belongs inside a content-hashed artifact') from the bundle to the pages.

NOT FIXED HERE: build.gitSha, same file, same page. It changes on every commit regardless of relevance, so it costs early cutoff across commits — a cost, not a correctness problem, on an orphan diagnostic page. Flagged rather than silently changed, because removing it removes real diagnostic value.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build twice with a fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH produces a byte-identical _site; a skipped-bundle build and a Vite-ran build still produce identical trees; npm test and npm run test:data pass on Node 24.18.
close_reason:
Landed 5851f365. emptyOutDir:false + build-app.mjs owns cleaning on every path (clean -> maybe-vite -> prune-unnamed -> touch); _data/build.js honors SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH.

THE VERIFICATION THAT MATTERS: two builds at a fixed epoch are now byte-identical across the WHOLE of _site including _scaffold-check, and the same comparison spans a Vite-ran and a Vite-skipped build. ADR 0019 had to assert that property by careful mirroring of two code paths; it now holds by construction because there is one path.

The stale-chunk hazard emptyOutDir existed to prevent is covered on the Vite path, which never pruned before: a real source change rotating app-entry-B7KwfIe3 -> app-entry-CHv4yfJX left 15 assets, not 16. A planted stale chunk + empty nested dir were also pruned.

npm test 1076 / test:data 1209+2 skipped / smoke passed, on Node 24.18 (default in a stelis session is 26 — must nvm use first).

LEFTOVER, deliberate: build.gitSha still changes per commit, costing cutoff across commits (not determinism within one) on an orphan diagnostic page.

title: Prime flow: priming in a Safari tab is discarded when the user installs the PWA
description:
Uncovered by the beeatlas-93t device run (iOS 18.7). An installed PWA gets its OWN storage bucket, separate from the Safari tab on the same origin — confirmed by writing a Cache Storage marker in one context and reading it in the other, in both directions. So a user who runs the offline prime in Safari (occurrences DB ~33 MB + data artifacts) and THEN adds the app to the Home Screen silently re-downloads everything, with no indication why.

Also measured: navigator.storage.persist() is GRANTED in the installed app and DENIED in Safari, so tab-primed data is not protected from pressure eviction either.

Pre-existing — not introduced by the basemap work — but the basemap makes it much more expensive (238 MB rather than 33 MB), so beeatlas-6rs will gate the BASEMAP download on being installed. This issue is the smaller, separate question of what the EXISTING prime flow should do: steer to install first, warn, or silently accept the re-download.
acceptance_criteria: Decide and implement the behavior for priming outside an installed context; whatever is chosen, the user is not silently charged twice.

title: Basemap: migration ADR, supersede ADR 0001, drop the mapbox SW route
description:
Ship with the swap. Write the migration ADR (MapLibre + self-hosted Protomaps PMTiles): records OSM/ODbL + Protomaps attribution obligations, the separate artifact hosting decision, the glyph-range completeness rule, and where a future multi-region seam goes. Mark docs/adr/0001-mapbox-basemap-cache.md as superseded — never delete (CLAUDE.md convention); its whole subject (a <=30-day Mapbox perf cache under Product Terms 2.8.1) ceases to exist once we self-host, and offline caching becomes unrestricted.

Delete the mapbox-basemap StaleWhileRevalidate route (src/sw.ts:96-128) and add an activation-time caches.delete('mapbox-basemap') so devices with the old cache reclaim the space. Remove mapbox-gl from package.json.
acceptance_criteria: ADR 0001 marked superseded with a pointer; new ADR merged; sw.ts route gone; old cache deleted on activate; no mapbox-gl in package.json.
notes:
DECISIONS MADE IN beeatlas-q73 THAT STILL NEED RECORDING — the swap shipped 2026-08-01 without its ADR, so this issue owns writing them up, not just superseding 0001.

1. MapLibre's worker is served from the page tree, not bundled. It locates itself by deriving a sibling URL off its own import.meta.url, which no bundler can preserve; bundled, it 404s and reports NOTHING (tiles hang in 'loading', map 'load' never fires, blank map, clean console). Eleventy copies it + maplibre-gl-shared.mjs out of node_modules to /basemap/maplibre/ and bee-map calls setWorkerUrl. REJECTED: `?worker&url` (Vite emits a chunk it leaves out of the manifest, so the asset prune deletes it) and a side-effect-only import (tree-shaken to 0 bytes — maplibre-gl marks its dist side-effect-free while the worker self-installs with a bare assignment). Pinned by src/tests/maplibre-worker.test.ts.

2. The style is fetched data, and the map does not wait for it. Archives are date-stamped for the grace period, so the manifest must be fetched to learn the current filename. The map is constructed synchronously with a blank style (which still carries glyphs, or the occurrence labels vanish) and setStyle swaps in the real basemap when the manifest resolves. An earlier cut awaited the manifest before constructing anything, which put the map chrome and the offline GPS behind a network request — wrong, per LOC-01 SC-2.

3. The click chain is one ordered hit-test, because MapLibre has no addInteraction. The property that made the Mapbox chain correct was never explicit: queryRenderedFeatures only returns features from RENDERED layers, so visibility:none layers are skipped without a check.

4. Occurrence labels use Noto Sans Medium. Under Mapbox they asked for 'Open Sans Bold', which the hosted style served; self-hosted glyphs mean an unshipped stack 404s and the label silently disappears. No Bold is vendored.

ADR 0001 is marked Obsolete as of 2026-08-01 with a pointer here; this issue still owns the formal supersession.
ADDED BY beeatlas-8py (hillshade, shipped 2026-08-02). Decisions made there that want an ADR, since they are all 'we measured, then chose against the obvious option':

1. TERRAIN IS A SEPARATE ARCHIVE from the vector basemap, publishing independently through a MERGED manifest. Rejected: one combined archive (couples two very different refresh cadences) and a second manifest file (two things to keep in sync).
2. ELEVATION IS QUANTIZED TO 1 m AND ENCODED AS LOSSLESS WEBP. This is 200 MB -> 61 MB with a worst-case error of 0.496 m, and it is the only reason a z11 pyramid is affordable. Rejected: raw PNG (200 MB), 4 m quantum (same size as WebP but actually lossy), any lossy codec (it would invent terrain).
3. MAXZOOM 11 PAIRED WITH A FADE TO ZERO BY z13.5. The fade is what makes the cheap DEM sufficient. Rejected: z10 (21.9 MB, but ridges smear at z12 — screenshot comparison drove this) and z13 (~1 GB).
4. THE LAYER SITS UNDER THE water FILL, not under the first symbol layer as beeatlas-8py specified. protomaps-themes-base interleaves fills and lines; its first symbol layer is index 57, so 'under the labels' would wash every road, trail and stream.

Also still true and still wanted here: docs/adr/0001-mapbox-basemap-cache.md is superseded, and src/sw.ts's api.mapbox.com route is dead code.
close_reason: ADR 0026 written (MapLibre + self-hosted Protomaps, incl. the beeatlas-8py terrain decisions); ADR 0001 formally superseded and kept for its record of why offline was never licensable under Mapbox; api.mapbox.com route deleted and the orphaned mapbox-basemap cache now deleted on SW activate. Verified against the built worker; three tests pin it. mapbox-gl was already out of package.json as of beeatlas-q73.

title: Update toast reloads before the new SW takes control, so the reload serves old data
description:
REPORTED 2026-08-01 (user, real-world): on a slow cellular link, tapping "A data update
is available — tap to reload" WHILE THE PAGE IS STILL LOADING reloads the page but comes
back on the OLD data. Letting the original load finish and then tapping works.

CONFIRMED IN CODE (not yet reproduced on-device):

src/bee-atlas.ts:1303 —
    private _onBannerTap = () => {
      const wb = (window as ...).__wb;
      wb?.messageSkipWaiting();
      window.location.reload();
    };

messageSkipWaiting() only POSTS {type:'SKIP_WAITING'} to the waiting worker. The handler
(src/sw.ts:132) then calls self.skipWaiting() asynchronously; the new worker must
activate and take over this client before a reload is served new assets. The reload here
fires synchronously on the SAME TICK as the post, so it races activation and normally
loses. The old worker serves the reload -> old precached shell. The new worker activates
moments later, which is exactly why a SECOND tap (or a tap after the page settles) works.

A slow link widens the window two ways: the in-flight loads keep the old worker busy
handling fetches, delaying its message processing; and the whole navigation is slower.

Nothing anywhere listens for workbox-window's `controlling` event —
`grep -rn "controlling" src/` returns only an unrelated comment. The documented
workbox-window recipe is the inverse order: register the `controlling` listener FIRST,
then messageSkipWaiting(), and reload only when control has actually transferred.

The existing test (src/tests/cache-state.test.ts:449) asserts only that
messageSkipWaiting is called and explicitly punts on reload ("Soft assert on reload —
may fail in some happy-dom versions", with an empty if-body), so the ordering was never
pinned. Any fix should close that too.

FIX DIRECTION:
    const reload = onceGuard(() => window.location.reload());
    wb.addEventListener('controlling', reload);
    wb.messageSkipWaiting();
    setTimeout(reload, ~3000);   // fallback

Three cases the fix must keep working, all currently handled by the unconditional reload:
  - no __wb at all (SW unsupported / registration failed) -> reload immediately;
  - no worker actually waiting (banner stale, user tapped twice) -> `controlling` never
    fires, so the timeout fallback is what keeps the button from being dead;
  - the reload must fire exactly once (guard the listener + timeout against both firing).

NOTE on scope: `controlling` also fires when ANOTHER tab triggers skipWaiting (the
'waiting' handler in src/sw-registration.ts:26 already notes event.isExternal). Attaching
the listener inside the tap handler — rather than globally in sw-registration.ts — keeps
an external update from silently reloading a tab the user is working in.

OPEN QUESTION: worth confirming the data actually comes from the precached shell rather
than from manifest.json. manifest.json is NetworkFirst ('data-manifest', src/manifest.ts:38)
and self-primes into Cache Storage, so a reload SHOULD refetch it even under the old
worker — which would mean the stale part is the app bundle / precached shell, not the
data files. Diagnosis of the race is solid either way, but the "old data" phrasing
deserves a check against which layer is actually stale before declaring it fixed.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-01 in 227d75c8.

OPEN QUESTION FROM THE FILING — RESOLVED. The stale layer is the APP SHELL, not the data
files. vite.sw.config.ts globIgnores 'data/**', so the precache is only app/index.html +
assets/**/*.{js,css,wasm}. But src/sw.ts registers a NavigationRoute bound to the
precached /app/index.html for every /app/ navigation — so a reload served by the OLD
worker returns the old index.html, which references the old hashed bundle. manifest.json
(NetworkFirst, self-priming) would still have refetched fine; it is the shell that was
stale, and the observable is that the app comes back unchanged with the banner still
there.

FIX: listen for workbox-window's `controlling` FIRST, messageSkipWaiting() second, reload
only on control transfer. Listener attached inside the handler, not globally in
sw-registration.ts, so an update taken in ANOTHER tab (`controlling` fires there too —
cf. the isExternal note on the 'waiting' handler) cannot reload a tab in use.

THREE PRESERVED BEHAVIOURS the unconditional reload got right:
 - no __wb (index.html mounts <bee-atlas> with no SW; registration failed) -> immediate
   reload, nothing to wait for;
 - nothing actually waiting / message never processed -> 3s backstop reload, so the
   button is never dead. Worst case = the old behaviour, not worse;
 - exactly one reload (listener + timeout share a `reloaded` guard).

The in-handler `_reloadPending` guard is NOT redundant with the button's disabled state:
`cache-update-acted` from the account menu is wired to the same handler
(bee-atlas connectedCallback) and re-enters, bypassing the button. A mutation sweep
caught this — removing the guard passed until a test drove that second route.

UI: the button reads busy (disabled + aria-busy) while waiting. The wait lands exactly
when the link is slow, and a silent button is what the bug felt like; no new visual
pattern, just the standard disabled state.

TEST DEBT REPAID. The predecessor test (cache-state.test.ts) asserted only
"messageSkipWaiting was called" — which is TRUE under the broken code — and wrapped every
reload assertion in `if (reloadSpy)` with an empty body, so it would have gone silently
vacuous if the stub ever broke. That is how a reload-ordering bug survived in a tested
file. Now 5 tests asserting the ORDER, with stubReload() unconditional so an environment
that cannot stub fails loudly instead of passing emptily.

MUTATION SWEEP, all 4 caught: same-tick reload (the original bug) -> 2 fail; no timeout
backstop -> 1 fail; no !wb immediate reload -> 1 fail; no re-entry guard -> 1 fail.

NOT DONE / NOT REPRODUCED: no on-device slow-link verification. The race is confirmed
structurally and by mutation, but the real-world confirmation is the next cellular
update-tap. Worth a mention if it recurs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ecdysis probe must write the Stelis boundary receipt
description:
The Stelis half of the change-probe thread (st-8bj, CLOSED 2026-07-24) shipped a
cross-repo contract that BeeAtlas never fulfils, so it is dead code in production.

CONTRACT (from st-8bj notes): on a 'boundary run Stelis sets env
STELIS_BOUNDARY_RECEIPT=<path>, clears any stale receipt first, and reads it back
after a clean exit. A probing loader that short-circuits an unchanged source writes
JSON there:
    {"unchanged": bool (required), "records": int|null, "since": string|null}
Stelis records it as a source-report on the trace and surfaces it in --explain --last,
run-plan narration, and the --explain/--why boundary line. A missing or unparseable
receipt is SILENT (no annotation), never an error — which is why this gap has been
invisible.

GAP: `grep -rn STELIS_BOUNDARY_RECEIPT data/` returns nothing. `ecdysis` IS a boundary
task (stelis src/beeatlas.rkt:540) so the env var is set every run; maderas runs stelis
eb0349a, which has the contract deployed. We just never write the file.

EVIDENCE (nightly 2026-07-31 03:00, maderas): the skip surfaced only as the loader's
own raw print —
    ecdysis │   Ecdysis source unchanged since last pull (change-probe); reusing cached ZIP
  ≡ outputs identical to last build — early cutoff
"outputs identical" is the ONLY thing Stelis can say, exactly as stelis src/cache.rkt:110
predicts: a loader that short-circuits never touches its outputs, so output-delta can
only ever report 'identical — it cannot report WHY. So beeatlas-29j's probe is still
"reusing a cache behind Stelis's back", the precise condition st-8bj existed to end.

FIX: in ecdysis_pipeline._download_zip, on the probe-skip branch, write the receipt to
os.environ["STELIS_BOUNDARY_RECEIPT"] when that var is set. The data is already in hand
at that point — _probe_says_unchanged has the sidecar's `since`, and `records` is 0 by
construction on the skip path (that IS the skip condition). Best-effort like the rest of
the probe: a write failure must never break the load. Consider also emitting
{"unchanged": false, ...} on the download path so --why can distinguish "probe said
changed" from "loader predates the probe" — st-8bj treats a missing receipt as
indistinguishable from a plain run.

Worth an integration-ish test that the JSON matches the three-field shape stelis
boundary-report-test.rkt asserts; the fields are a cross-repo contract, so a typo here
degrades silently rather than failing.

Depends on nothing — Stelis side is deployed and ready.
notes:
SHIPPED 2026-07-31 in 715584c5.

Loader now writes the receipt on both conclusive paths:
  skip  -> {"unchanged": true,  "records": 0, "since": <sidecar since>}
  pull  -> {"unchanged": false, "records": <new since baseline>|null, "since": ...}
Silence (no write) when STELIS_BOUNDARY_RECEIPT is unset or the probe reached no
conclusion (no baseline / API down) — Stelis reads that as "said nothing", never an
error. The cache-fallback path (download failed, serving stale cache) also stays silent.

SHAPE VERIFIED AGAINST STELIS'S ACTUAL READER, not just st-8bj's notes
(stelis/src/exec.rkt read-boundary-receipt, ~line 263):
  - 'unchanged required + must be boolean, else the whole receipt is #f
  - records: (and (exact-nonnegative-integer? records) records) — JSON null -> 'null ->
    #f. Our max(0, delta) is always a nonneg int, and we emit null only on the
    deliberately-unquantified total-moved path.
  - since:   (and (string? since) since) — null -> #f.
Stelis creates the receipt's parent dir (make-directory* at exec.rkt:409) and deletes
any stale receipt before the run, so a plain write_text suffices and we cannot misread
a prior run's report.

Probe reworked from `_probe_says_unchanged -> bool` to `_probe_source -> SourceReport |
None` (frozen dataclass, JSON shape = the cross-repo contract) since the receipt made
the probe's numbers a second consumer. None = no conclusion.

CAUGHT WHILE WRITING THE TESTS: the refactor briefly let the report's max(0, delta)
clamp leak into the SKIP DECISION, so a modified-since count that SHRANK (records
deleted from inside the `since` window — reachable via the documented compensating-
replace blind spot) would have read as unchanged. Decision now turns on equality
(delta == 0), matching the original prototype; only the reported quantity is clamped.

7 receipt tests + a direct no-env-var test (pins that absent the env var nothing is
written ANYWHERE — a run-level test only sees its own tmp dir and would miss a default
path). 5-mutation sweep, all caught.

ALSO IN THIS COMMIT, from the two-axis review of 145ee1ae:
 - _write_probe_baseline back to catching Exception (I had narrowed it to OSError; it
   runs AFTER the ZIP is committed, so a raise there fails a successful download).
 - ECDYSIS_SKIP_PROBE=0 now silences the probe ENTIRELY (it still ran the baseline read,
   so the revert switch left v2-API traffic in place — useless when the API is the
   problem). Pinned with api.calls == [].
 - api fixture is autouse (opt-in re-opened the live-network trap the prior commit fixed).
 - ADR 0023 added; data/README.md points at it and no longer quotes an unconditional
   90-115s for the ecdysis stage.

NOT YET OBSERVED IN A REAL STELIS RUN — the contract is verified against the reader's
source, but the "↺ source unchanged — ingestion skipped" line lands in tonight's nightly
(maderas runs stelis eb0349a, which has the reader). Worth a glance at
~/beeatlas-nightly.log tomorrow; no action expected.
close_reason: Closed

description: The WABA checklist species list carried 'bombus lapponicus' (Palearctic) while its 145 checklist records were already filed under 'bombus sylvicola', so the atlas published a ghost lapponicus page with zero of everything and sylvicola showed on_checklist=false. Added the synonym to occurrence_synonyms; needed a species_traits tiebreak fix first (Bee-Gap carries both names and its lapponicus row says 'introduced'). Guarded by assert_no_synonym_survives_as_species.

description: Both sides assign hue = position in a sorted member list, but _data/species.js used occurrence_count > 0 while data/species_maps.py used occurrence_count > 0 OR on_checklist. occurrence_count is the Ecdysis specimen arm only, so specimen-less-but-plotting species (Chelostoma phaceliae: 1 iNat obs + 2 checklist points) were greyed AND every later species was shifted one hue. 187 of 553 dot-drawing species across 31 genera were affected. title: Extend header search past label numbers: taxa, places, people
description:
The header search field (beeatlas-v66) routes every query through _onSearchSubmit in bee-atlas, which today knows only the catalog lookup. Add resolvers for taxa, places and people, plus a result list in the popover for when a query is ambiguous across kinds (a label number is unique; a name is not).

Open questions: ranking across kinds, whether a taxon hit is a filter (it is a view of the data) while a specimen hit is a selection (ADR 0020), and whether picking a place sets bounds or a place filter.
design:
Designed 2026-08-03 → docs/adr/0028-a-search-result-is-a-record-or-a-view.md (Proposed).

Thesis: every search result names either a RECORD or a VIEW. A record is selected
(label number — ADR 0020, unchanged); a view is filtered (taxon, person, place,
county, ecoregion each set their own FilterState dimension).

The three open questions, answered:
 - Taxon hit = FILTER (it names a set, not a record).
 - Place hit = the PLACE FILTER, not bounds (occurrence_places membership; a bbox
   would re-admit non-members and the checklist rows filter.ts:530 drops).
 - Ranking = syntax first (digits ⇒ label number, exclusively), then match quality
   (exact/prefix/word-prefix/substring), then weight (record count), then label.
   Kind is a group heading, NOT a ranking key.

Also decided:
 - As-you-type combobox over an in-memory index; numeric queries stay submit-only
   (one speculative row, SQL runs on pick). No SQL per keystroke.
 - Search COMPOSES with the active filter and replaces only the dimension it names.
 - Search fits the camera to the result extent (from queryVisibleGeoJSON, no extra
   query); zero matches ⇒ no move. The panel still never moves the camera.
 - A row carries a trailing page link (species/place/collector) as an ATTRIBUTE, not
   a second row — page existence is not derivable (src/taxon-pages.ts).
 - Rows are buttons in the existing role=dialog popover, not an ARIA listbox (a
   listbox option cannot contain the page link).
 - search-submit retires in favour of search-query {query} + search-pick {candidate};
   candidates are declarative data, ranked by a pure src/search.ts. searchStatus stays.

Known follow-on work: places.json hoists from <bee-pane> to <bee-atlas>; <bee-map>
gains a fitBounds property; inputmode="numeric" goes.
close_reason: Closed

title: manifest generated_at is the site-build clock, so a code deploy fakes data freshness
description:
The header/menu freshness label renders generated_at as DATA age ('Today', 'Data as of Jul 12, 2026' — src/manifest.ts formatFreshness). Before the Model Y cutover (fae1dbd0) generated_at was stamped once, inside the nightly's data-publish leg (data/nightly.sh: --meta generated_at=$(_ts)). Now scripts/postbuild-data.mjs:112-113 stamps it from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, which every publish path sets to its own wall clock (nightly.sh:114, publish-code.sh:54, publish-notes.sh:65). So a code-only deploy or a single note publish resets the 'data as of' clock without touching the data.

Evidence 2026-07-31: live manifest generated_at = 2026-07-31T20:04:29Z, ~1 min after commit 44e30c2b (a build fix, 13:03 PDT) — a publish-code.sh run, not a data refresh. If the nightly broke for a week, pushing code would still make the header say 'Today'.

publish-code.sh:52-54 documents the choice deliberately; the defect is the mismatch with what the UI claims. Fix direction: carry a data timestamp with the export (or have the code/note publish paths preserve the previous manifest's generated_at) and keep SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH for build determinism only.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-01 in 33e84b86.

SEMANTICS CHOSEN (user call): "last successful REFRESH", not "last content change". A
healthy nightly that finds nothing new still means the data was checked today; a label
drifting to "5 days ago" through a quiet spell would misreport staleness in the other
direction. The rejected alternative was content-derived (carry the previous manifest's
generated_at forward when all 7 runtime-artifact hashes match) — self-maintaining and
needing no pipeline coupling, but it reads as stale during a quiet-but-healthy stretch.

MECHANISM: scripts/fetch-data.sh writes $EXPORT_DIR/generated_at (epoch seconds) after a
successful FULL run; scripts/postbuild-data.mjs reads it via lib/data-freshness.js
instead of stamping SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH. Code and note publishes rebuild against an
unchanged export and inherit the stamp untouched. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH stays for build
determinism only; all three publish scripts' comments updated to say so.

TWO BOUNDARIES that took deciding:
 - A SCOPED stelis run must not stamp. publish-notes.sh calls
   `fetch-data.sh --from notes-harvest notes`, and notes render into static pages, not
   into lib/runtime-artifacts.js — so the stamp is gated on `--all`. (Also settled the
   question I'd flagged as needing a design call: notes never change what the label
   describes, and the label doesn't render on static pages at all — bee-header.ts passes
   null there. So both non-data publish paths simply preserve.)
 - Absent/unparseable stamp -> the "local" sentinel (client hides it, D-12), NOT the
   current time. Falling back to now is the original bug one layer down.

WHY lib/: postbuild-data.mjs hardcodes _site/data and rmSync's it, so invoking it from a
test would delete real build output. The derivation moved to lib/data-freshness.js
(same pattern as lib/build-data-dir.js, lib/runtime-artifacts.js) and is unit-tested in
src/tests/data-freshness.test.ts — 10 tests, incl. the handoff to formatFreshness so the
sentinel is pinned to render as NO label rather than a wrong date.

VERIFIED end-to-end by running the real script against a temp EXPORT_DIR:
  stamped   -> generated_at: 2026-08-01T10:07:02.000Z
  unstamped -> generated_at: local

DEPLOY ORDERING (done): the export dir needed a stamp BEFORE this code ships, or the
label would vanish until the next nightly. Backfilled on maderas to 1785578822
(2026-08-01T10:07:02Z) = the mtime of the newest runtime artifact from today's nightly,
