title: Move the build id out of the bundle and into the slim manifest
description:
Found while reviewing the beeatlas-bon bundle gate (Fable review, 2026-07-31).

vite.config.ts defines __APP_VERSION__ from `git rev-parse HEAD` + a tracked-dirty flag, and it is `define`d — so it lands INSIDE a content-hashed chunk (bee-header's "Build <id>" menu row). Consequence: any commit that touches nothing the bundle depends on — docs, data/, eleventy.config.js, a test — still changes the emitted bee-header chunk.

That forced beeatlas-bon's gate to fingerprint git HEAD, because otherwise it would skip Vite while `vite build` would have produced something different, and the "Build <id>" popover — whose entire purpose is telling you which code an installed PWA is running — would name a commit that is not deployed.

The cost is most of the gate's value: the bundle now rebuilds on every commit, so a skip only happens on a nightly where nothing landed at all.

THE FIX, which is also the principle beeatlas-96m established and stopped one step short of: a build identifier does not belong inside a content-hashed artifact. Move it to the slim manifest (scripts/postbuild-data.mjs), which is served no-cache and already carries generated_at for exactly this reason, and have bee-header read it the way it already reads the freshness label — via src/manifest.ts, which is fetched at runtime.

Then:
  - the bundle is a function of src/ + configs + deps + .env alone, so the gate skips whenever those are unchanged (the common nightly case) and drops git HEAD from its fingerprint;
  - the build id becomes MORE honest, not less: it is regenerated on every publish rather than frozen into a chunk that may be reused;
  - 96m's rule holds completely — nothing clock- or HEAD-derived is left in a hashed chunk.

Touches: vite.config.ts (drop the define + buildVersion), src/manifest.ts (add the field), src/bee-header.ts (read it from the manifest instead of the compile-time const, keeping the 'dev' fallback), scripts/postbuild-data.mjs + scripts/make-local-manifest.js (emit it), lib/runtime-artifacts.js's Manifest contract, and scripts/build-app.mjs (delete buildIdInputs). Note bee-header currently reads BUILD_VERSION synchronously at module scope; the manifest is async, so the row needs the same not-yet-loaded handling the freshness label has.
acceptance_criteria: __APP_VERSION__ is gone from the bundle; the Build row reads the id from manifest.json; scripts/build-app.mjs no longer fingerprints git HEAD, and two builds of one tree at different commits produce identical asset filenames.
close_reason:
Done and verified live. __APP_VERSION__ is gone from the bundle; build_id travels in the slim manifest (postbuild-data writes it, loadBuildId reads it, bee-atlas passes it to bee-header as a property). vite.config.ts now has no `define` at all.

AC met: two builds with different GITHUB_SHA produced build_id 72ae32e -> deadbee with all 15 asset filenames IDENTICAL — the gate reusing the bundle across a commit, which it could never do before. Confirmed in the browser during the beeatlas-8zs UAT: bee-header's buildId equals /data/manifest.json's build_id.

HONEST CAVEAT, from review: this is a TRADE, not a strict improvement, and ADR 0019's first draft said otherwise. Baked in, the id travelled with the code and so named what you were RUNNING — the row's original purpose, diagnosing a stale installed PWA. From the manifest, over NetworkFirst, it names the latest publish the client can REACH. Right for "what is deployed", wrong for the stale-install case. Corrected in the ADR; beeatlas-4zu tracks the honest replacement (the running chunk's own content hash).

Static pages lose the Build row — their bee-header entry imports no manifest because those pages fetch nothing on paint, matching the freshness row's long-standing behaviour.

SPUN OUT: a real defect in the beeatlas-96m clock guard shipped earlier the same day. Its block-comment strip ran between two unrelated glob strings ('**/_site/**' supplies both a /* and a */), cutting vite.config.ts from 11,274 chars to 1,115 — so the guard inspected a tenth of the file. My original negative test passed only because the tamper was appended at the END, past the last */. Fixed (line comments only) and both guards re-tested by tampering mid-file.

title: Quick lookup: find a specimen by catalog/label number
description:
Curators and collectors working from a physical label need to jump straight to the specimen record from the number printed on the label. Today the only route is to load the map/table and filter, which is slow and non-obvious.

Wanted: type (or paste) a catalog/label number somewhere prominent and land on that specimen.

Data already present: `catalog_number` is a contracted column on `marts/occurrences` (data/dbt/models/marts/schema.yml) and is already carried through to the frontend Occurrence type (src/filter.ts:53) and the free-text search field list (src/filter.ts:98). So this is likely a UX/entry-point problem, not a data problem.
design:
## Shape (settled 2026-07-31)

**An additional input field in the sidebar that SELECTS, not filters.** On submit, resolve the typed number to its `occ_id` and open that specimen's detail card via the existing `selectedOccIds` path. This preserves the filter-vs-selection separation established in Phase 999.8 (bounds are a filter; individual records are a selection) and keeps `FilterState` untouched — no new required field, no cascade through every FilterState literal.

## Where it goes

`src/bee-pane.ts`. Add a `_renderCatalog()` peer to the five existing section renderers and slot it into `_renderListContent` (:1223-1227, which composes What / Who / Where / When / Tiers).

Reuse the established `filter-row` markup verbatim — `row-icon` SVG + `.input-group` > `.input-wrap` > `input.filter-input` — as used by `_renderWhat` (:938) and `_renderWho` (:986). No new UI pattern.

`bee-pane` is a pure presenter: it emits an event upward; `bee-atlas` owns the state and performs the selection.

## Input format (verified against data/beeatlas.duckdb, ecdysis_data.occurrences)

Users type the **full numeric label number, without the `WSDA_` prefix**.

- All 46,090 catalogued rows match `WSDA_<digits>` — one prefix corpus-wide.
- Suffixes are 7-8 digits, no leading zeros, and **1:1 with catalog_number** (46,090 distinct for 46,090 rows, zero collisions) — a bare integer is unambiguous, so exactly one record resolves.
- All 46,090 have coordinates, so anything that resolves is reachable on the map.

Parse as an integer, tolerating a pasted `WSDA_` prefix and stray whitespace. Match against `regexp_extract(catalog_number, '[0-9]+$', 0)` — the same identity notion the pipeline already uses to join specimens to iNat's WABA catalog-suffix field (`int_ecdysis_catalog_suffixes.sql`, `int_ecdysis_base.sql:42`). Do not build a second one.

The client already carries `catalog_number` as a string (`OccurrenceRow.catalog_number`, filter.ts:53; present in `OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS`, :98). Match client-side with a suffix regexp first — 46k rows is small — and only export a numeric `catalog_suffix` column if that measures slow.

Do NOT overload the bare integer to also mean `ecdysis:<n>`. `ecdysis_id` and catalog suffix are different numbers; conflating them silently mis-resolves.

## Defaults for the small stuff (change only with reason)

- **Scope:** catalog suffix only. `fieldNumber` is not in scope — revisit if users ask.
- **Miss case:** show an inline "no specimen with that number" message in the field; do not clear the map state or the current selection.
- **Offline:** the PWA already caches occurrence data, so this should work offline for free. Confirm during UAT; don't design for it.

## Constraint

Static hosting on the read path — the lookup resolves against the client-side occurrence store (wa-sqlite + hyparquet), never a server endpoint.

## Verification

UAT via the `run-app` skill. Specimen selection is already drivable headlessly through the `o=<ids>&pane=list` URL param, which gives a known-good `occ_id` to check the typed-number path against.
acceptance_criteria: Given a catalog/label number from a physical specimen label, a user can reach that specimen's detail view in one step, without panning the map or hand-building a filter.
notes:
UAT DONE 2026-07-31 via the run-app skill, at http://localhost:8080/ against real local data (98,763 rows, 46,092 catalogued). Driven in Chrome by typing into the field, not by setting state.

The field is where the design said: first row of the Filters panel, tag icon, placeholder "Label number — press Enter", aria-label "Find a specimen by its catalog or label number", inputmode=numeric, wearing the filter-row costume like its neighbours.

  1. TYPED "2303966" + Enter -> URL became o=ecdysis%3A5594056, "1 selected", detail card
     (29 IV 2023, Richard Williams, Lasioglossum), map recentred to z12.
     This is the bead's own prescribed verification: the DB says WSDA_2303966 = ecdysis_id
     5594056, so the typed-number path landed on exactly the record the known-good
     o=<occId> path would have.
  2. TYPED "9999999" -> inline "No specimen with number 9999999" AND the previous
     selection survived intact (still 1 selected, same card, o= unchanged, map unmoved).
     Exactly the specified miss behaviour: "do not clear the map state or the current
     selection."
  3. PASTED "  WSDA_2303969 " (prefix + leading/trailing whitespace) -> o=ecdysis:5594059.
     Prefix and whitespace tolerance confirmed against real data.
  4. TYPED "5594056" — a real ecdysis_id, NOT a catalog suffix -> MISS, previous selection
     preserved. The prohibition holds: "Do NOT overload the bare integer to also mean
     ecdysis:<n>." (An earlier attempt with WSDA_2303970 also missed; checked the DB
     first — that number genuinely does not exist, the run stops at ...969. Not a defect.)

NOT VERIFIED: the offline case. The bead defers it ("the PWA already caches occurrence
data, so this should work offline for free. Confirm during UAT; don't design for it"),
and it needs more than the dev server: the SW only registers on /app/, and in dev the
built SW is not active, so a real test means a production build served statically, an
/app/ visit to precache, then killing the server. Worth doing because it is exactly the
path the beeatlas-8zs review fix addresses — a failed lookup now reports "Couldn't look
that up just now" instead of falsely claiming the specimen does not exist. Until then,
offline behaviour is assumed, not shown.
close_reason: Closed

title: Bundle hashes change on every build: __APP_VERSION__ bakes in a wall-clock minute
description:
Found 2026-07-31 while verifying beeatlas-4oa's "identical to a full build" property on maderas: two full builds of the SAME source produced different chunk hashes, and the only difference in the rendered page was asset URLs (bee-header-B3Zo1LVX -> bee-header-53OCcjQY, taxon-page-WmAm9HY_ -> taxon-page-b0uZJCii, ...).

CAUSE: vite.config.ts buildVersion() (~line 18) composes __APP_VERSION__ from the git short sha AND `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 16)` — a wall-clock stamp at MINUTE resolution. It is `define`d, so it is baked into the bundle. Any two builds in different minutes therefore differ in content, and content-hashed filenames change with them.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is the part that matters: every nightly ships an entirely new set of asset URLs even when no source changed. Returning visitors re-download the whole bundle (bee-atlas alone is ~2 MB / 560 kB gzip), and the service worker re-precaches every asset — nightly, forever, for nothing. Hashed filenames exist precisely so unchanged code keeps its URL and stays cached; a build clock defeats that. It also violates stelis DESIGN's "content-addressed, not timestamped" principle in the one place the site actually publishes URLs.

NOT a beeatlas-4oa defect — the scoped render is exactly right. With the bundle held fixed (full build, then a scoped render against that same manifest), the scoped page is byte-identical to the full build's, verified on maderas. This bead is about the bundle, and it predates that work.

FIX SHAPE: keep the sha, drop the clock — __APP_VERSION__ = the short sha alone, which is what actually identifies the code. If a human-readable build time is wanted in the UI, source it from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (already exported by the nightly and publish-notes.sh, and already the determinism clock per ADR 0004) rather than `new Date()`, and prefer putting it somewhere that is NOT baked into a hashed chunk — the slim manifest already carries generated_at for exactly this purpose.

VERIFY BY: build twice without touching src/, and compare `ls _site/assets/`. Today the names change; they should not. Worth adding as a determinism assertion once fixed — the same "build twice, compare hashes" harness stelis uses (--verify).
acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive full builds of unchanged source produce identical asset filenames.
close_reason: Fixed and verified. buildVersion() baked a minute-resolution wall clock into the define'd __APP_VERSION__, so every build minted new chunk hashes and each nightly republished the whole bundle for unchanged source (~2 MB re-download + full SW re-precache, nightly). Now the short sha plus -dirty. Two builds 65s apart — crossing the boundary the bug needed — produce identical filenames for all 15 assets. Guarded by an arch.test.ts check negative-tested three ways (catches 'new Date(' and bare 'Date(', does not false-positive on 'formatDate('). Review found the dirty check ran only when GITHUB_SHA was absent (a CI build of a modified tree would claim a clean sha) and that untracked files made -dirty always-on; both fixed, and the marker's real precision — tracked-only, blind to gitignored inputs — is now stated rather than implied. Deployed to maderas.

title: Gate the Vite steps on src/ changing so a note publish skips them
description:
The acceptance criterion beeatlas-d3y did NOT meet, split out with a corrected value estimate.

d3y spec: "The Vite step is gated on src/ changing, so a note publish skips it entirely" / AC: "a note-only publish skips the Vite step." No gate was built. data/publish-notes.sh:88 still runs a full npm run build, which runs build:app and build:sw unconditionally.

WHY NOT DONE, AND WHY THIS IS NOW P3 RATHER THAN P1: the AC was written before the app build was measured. It assumed skipping the Vite step saved ~5s. After backend integration the app build is 0.59s and the SW pass ~0.9s, so gating saves ~1.5s of a 6.6s build. The 5s was not skipped for one caller, it was REMOVED for everyone -- the better outcome, and the reason the criterion is now worth little.

Deliberately deferred because:
  1. Small remaining win against a change to the PRODUCTION write path (st-nee: "do with fresh context").
  2. A naive skip is UNSOUND. If src/ changed, rendering against a stale manifest publishes stale assets. A correct gate compares src/ against what the stashed manifest was built from.
  3. Adding an unused build:content script ahead of its caller would be dead surface.

The mechanism is already in place: the manifest survives outside _site and outside node_modules, and a bare eleventy rerun works and is additive (verified -- assets preserved, hashed tags emitted). So this is only the gate plus the publish-notes.sh wiring.

See ADR 0016, "What this does NOT do". beeatlas-4oa (incremental render) is the larger remaining lever.
acceptance_criteria: A note-only publish skips build:app and build:sw, and a publish after a src/ change does NOT skip them.
notes:
LARGELY OVERTAKEN BY beeatlas-4oa (2026-07-31, PR #72). The note path no longer runs `npm run build` at all when the scoped render's precondition holds — it runs build:content (validate + eleventy + postbuild-data), which contains neither build:app nor build:sw. So the 3.47s this bead was priced at is already banked FOR THE NOTE PATH, and by a different mechanism than the one specified here.

What remains of this bead is the GENERAL gate: any full `npm run build` whose src/ is unchanged still rebuilds the bundle. The hard part is now done — scripts/build-receipt.mjs already fingerprints render code (incl. src/) and the Vite manifest, so "has src/ changed since the bundle that produced this manifest?" is a receipt component comparison rather than new machinery. This is mostly wiring plus deciding what a full build does when only src/ is unchanged.

Note the soundness worry recorded in the description ("a naive skip is UNSOUND — if src/ changed, rendering against a stale manifest publishes stale assets") is handled for the note path by the receipt: a src/ change moves the render fingerprint, --check fails, and publish-notes.sh falls back to a full build, which deploys the code.

Reprice before doing: against a note publish this is now worth ~0s, and against a nightly full build ~3.5s of a ~16s run that has 24h of headroom.
close_reason:
Delivered; ADR 0019. Note the bead's stated AC was already met by beeatlas-4oa — build:content contains neither bundle step, and a src/ change makes the receipt stale so the fallback runs both. This delivered the unstated remainder: gating the bundle INSIDE a full build.

build:app is now a gate (scripts/build-app.mjs) that reuses the bundle when src/, both Vite configs, package.json, package-lock.json, .env* and the build id are unchanged and every manifest-named asset is present. Reuse is only checkable because beeatlas-96m removed the build clock; the proof is a byte-comparison of a skipped build against a vite-ran build (1668 files identical, same 15 filenames, 2 MB main chunk identical; only _scaffold-check's builtAt differs, as it does between any two builds).

The work was not the skip but the three side effects a skip must impersonate:
  1. emptyOutDir was the CLEANING BOUNDARY (ADR 0016) — the only thing that deletes from _site, which merge-swap then makes authoritative for the live site via --delete. A skip cleans everything except assets/.
  2. It made assets look FRESH. merge-swap age-prunes assets at -mtime +30 on the stated assumption of "new URLs each publish"; a reused bundle keeps old mtimes and rsync -a preserves them, so after 30 days of skips the prune would delete the LIVE bundle nightly, with a green build and a healthy ping. Fixed by touching what is reused; verified locally (aged 40d -> 0 over 30d) AND on maderas through a real publish (0 served assets over 30 days), with the rsync leg confirmed empirically (a mtime-only change transfers, >f..t...., and the destination ends up fresh).
  3. It emptied assets/ itself. A skip now deletes unnamed files AND emptied directories, comparing FULL relative paths — basename-vs-top-level-entry would delete a nested assets/species/ right after the presence check vouched for it, which is not hypothetical (validate-bundle-size.mjs has a branch for that shape), and an empty species/ sends that validator down a chunk-less branch and fails the build.

Two reviewers, and both earned their place: CodeRabbit caught a Windows execFileSync issue; Fable caught the merge-swap mtime bug (high, invisible to any content comparison), .env being an unfingerprinted bundle input (VITE_MAPBOX_TOKEN — rotate it and the gate would serve the revoked one indefinitely), and the git-HEAD input. The path-aware prune has behavioural tests in lib/bundle-assets.js + src/tests/bundle-assets.test.ts, replacing a grep-for-an-identifier test that could not distinguish a function existing from a function being called.

7.03s -> 6.03s locally, ~2.2s on maderas. HONEST CAVEAT: __APP_VERSION__ is define'd from git HEAD, so any commit changes the bee-header chunk and the gate must fingerprint HEAD — meaning the saving only lands on builds where nothing shipped. beeatlas-4uj (move the build id into the slim manifest) is what makes it land on every full build including the fallback publish path, and it is 96m's principle one step further.

983 JS · 1099 with the data gate · typecheck 0 · deployed and verified on maderas.

title: Coalescing publish queue: N concurrent note writes collapse into one build
description:
Independent of the latency work, and also a blocker for inviting authors.

_publish_notes takes a flock and holds it for the whole build (~30s per api/main.py:360).
With one author that is invisible. With N authors the critical section serializes: the
second writer waits up to PUBLISH_LOCK_WAIT and then gets exit 75 -> 'publish deferred',
committed but not baked until something else picks it up. Throughput is roughly two
writes per minute, and the failure mode is hard to explain to an invited author.

Wanted: writes arriving during a build coalesce into ONE subsequent build covering all
of their keys, rather than queueing one build each. Reduces both worst-case wait and
total work. Note this is worth doing whatever the outcome of beeatlas-0gx - a faster
build shortens the critical section but does not make it concurrent.

Also revisit whether the POST must block on the publish at all; see the stelis-side
ADR 0007 amendment bead.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent note writes do not serialize behind one another's full builds, and no write ends in 'publish pending' under normal concurrency.
close_reason: Delivered; ADR 0018. Concurrent writers now share a build instead of each running one behind the flock. The soundness argument comes from 4oa: publish-notes.sh derives its keys from the committed store, so any build starting after my commit includes my note — which turns 'did my note publish?' into a question about ordering that a ticket counter answers. Builds are O(1) not O(N) (four concurrent writers cost two builds; forty also cost two) and the waiter's deadline is sized for two builds accordingly. The POST still blocks: coalescing removes the reason to revisit ADR 0007, since writers reach 'live' within a bounded wait instead of degrading into 'pending'. Two review passes hardened it — the running flag is lock-owned rather than inferred from Thread.is_alive(), every log goes through _safe_log (a raising logger would wedge the worker, or 500 a committed note from the request thread), and a failed Thread.start() degrades instead of raising. Concurrency is asserted with driven interleavings, not reasoned about. 148 API tests green; deployed and the service restarted.

title: Incremental eleventy render for note publishes
description:
Second step of beeatlas-0gx, only worth doing AFTER beeatlas-d3y (while Vite reprocesses every HTML file, rendering fewer pages saves nothing).

Once Eleventy is pure HTML generation, a note publish should render only the affected
species page(s) instead of all 1668. Measured cost of one species page: 2.4ms
(1396ms / 591 pages). Eleventy 3.x --incremental is the mechanism to evaluate.

Expected: ~9s -> ~3s on maderas. The residue is then eleventy startup + _data loading
(~1s local / ~2s maderas), not rendering - which is what makes the warm-process step
(beeatlas-0gx's third stage) the only way to go lower.

Stelis already computes WHICH species keys moved (STELIS_REBUILD_KEYS, st-pd1 / st-066),
so the key set is available at the publish boundary; this task is about the renderer
honoring it.
acceptance_criteria: A single-note publish renders only the affected species page(s), and the published site is identical to a full build.
notes:
CLOSED-OUT BY A REAL NOTE DELETION 2026-07-31. The user deleted a note on Bombus rufocinctus through the API, which exercised the one link that had never run end-to-end — and it happened to be the SUBTLEST arm, a REMOVED key rather than an added or changed one.

Observed, in order:
  1. notes-harvest pruned notes/"bombus rufocinctus.json" (4 files -> 3 in the export)
  2. --moved-keys notes  ->  stdout: bombus rufocinctus.json
     stderr: "notes — 1 of 4 keys: -bombus rufocinctus.json (build 35 vs 27)"
     The "-" marker is the removed arm. "build 35 vs 27" also demonstrates the `from`
     side being the previous OBSERVATION, not the previous build — 8 builds had run in
     between without re-producing notes.
  3. receipt check passed -> scoped path taken
  4. EXACTLY ONE file of 1690 re-rendered: _site/species/Bombus/rufocinctus/index.html
     (mtime 09:13:37; every other page still at 09:08:03 from the earlier full build)
  5. merge-swap published; the served page has 0 occurrences of "Community notes"

That the removed arm works is not an accident of the implementation: key-delta-moved
deliberately unions added+changed+REMOVED, because a deletion must re-render the page in
order for it to LOSE content. A design that scoped on added/changed only would have left
the deleted note visible until the next nightly.

IDENTITY, verified properly: comparing the scoped page against a fresh full build first
showed a difference — but only in asset URLs, because the bundle is not reproducible
across builds (vite.config.ts bakes a wall-clock minute into __APP_VERSION__; filed as
beeatlas-96m, a pre-existing bug that makes every nightly invalidate all client caches).
Holding the bundle fixed — full build, then a scoped render against that same manifest —
the pages are byte-identical (cmp), with notes correctly absent. So the AC holds; the
earlier mismatch was the bundle's nondeterminism, not the render's.

maderas left coherent: receipt current, _site complete, and every asset the served page
references exists in htdocs.
close_reason: Delivered and verified in production. A real note deletion on Bombus rufocinctus drove the full chain: harvest prune -> --moved-keys reporting the removed key -> receipt gate -> exactly 1 of 1690 pages re-rendered -> published without the note. Byte-identical to a full build when the bundle is held fixed. maderas: publish 23s (full fallback) / 8.5s (scoped); eleventy 10.45s -> 0.6s. Two prerequisites had to be fixed first, both found by deploying: publish-notes.sh not sharing the nightly's STELIS_STATE_DIR (which would have made this a no-op), and two stale .data.test.ts assertions that had been aborting the nightly. Spun out: beeatlas-96m (bundle hash churn), beeatlas-b4p (nightly builds the site twice).

title: Prune the build-tooling dependency tail
description:
Umbrella for trimming the tooling dependencies, which are where essentially all of the lockfile mass and all of the dependabot churn live.

Baseline measured 2026-07-30 from package-lock.json: 811 packages from 24 direct deps. The libraries doing actual application work — lit (6 reachable), mapbox-gl (1), wa-sqlite (1), @iarna/toml (1) — total 9 packages. Everything else is tooling.

Largest contributors:
  mapshaper                227 reachable / 217 exclusive   -> beeatlas-dqh
  vite-plugin-pwa          408 reachable (workbox-build 355) -> beeatlas-1dq
  @11ty/eleventy           130 / 115                        (load-bearing, not in scope)
  vitest                   100 / 25                         (load-bearing, not in scope)

Guiding rule: take the dependency when its value is fifteen years of accumulated bug fixes (mapshaper's topology simplification, workbox's offline runtime, mapbox-gl, wa-sqlite). Drop or vendor it when its value is only a convenient interface over something already understood.
acceptance_criteria:
- beeatlas-dqh, beeatlas-1dq, beeatlas-fa7 all closed or explicitly wontfix'd
- Lockfile package count re-measured and recorded here
- No regression in: npm test, npm run build, the nightly pipeline, cdk synth
notes:
PROGRESS 2026-07-30. Root lockfile 811 -> 594 packages (-217, -27%).

  beeatlas-dqh  CLOSED  3dfd7308  mapshaper -> data/package.json (-217)
  beeatlas-fa7  CLOSED  ceea0296  infra/ ts-node -> compiled dist/ (installed 30 -> 15)
  beeatlas-1dq  part 1 CLOSED f3387eea; part 2 open, re-scoped and gated on real-device iOS UAT

Lesson worth keeping: 'lockfile entries' is the wrong metric on its own. infra/'s entry count went UP (49 -> 52) while its INSTALLED count halved, because TypeScript 7 ships 20 os/cpu-gated native binary stubs of which exactly one ever installs. Measure installed packages when the answer will be used to justify a change.

Remaining mass in the root tree is vite-plugin-pwa/workbox-build (~400, see 1dq), @11ty/eleventy (~130) and vitest (~100). The latter two are load-bearing and out of scope.

title: Factor mapshaper out of the app's package.json into the data pipeline
description:
mapshaper is 27% of the app's dependency tree and is not used by the app.

Measured from package-lock.json (811 packages total, 24 direct deps):
  - mapshaper reaches 227 packages, 217 of them exclusively — the single largest contributor in the tree.
  - Its only consumer is data/topology_postprocess.py, invoked from data/nightly.sh. The site build never touches it.

NOT a rewrite. Topology-preserving simplification is exactly the kind of accumulated-bug-fixes dependency worth keeping — the problem is only that it lives in the app's dependency surface rather than the pipeline's.

Options to weigh:

  2. Pinned global/standalone install on maderas, referenced by absolute path from topology_postprocess.py.
  3. Vendor the mapshaper bundle (it ships a single-file CLI build).

Option 1 keeps the version pinned and reproducible in-repo and is probably the cleanest, but adds a second npm install to the nightly.

title: infra/: drop ts-node so TypeScript 7 can land
description:
Dependabot PR #55 (typescript ~6.0.3 -> ~7.0.2 in /infra) was rejected 2026-07-28 and the major is now ignored in .github/dependabot.yml.

Why it fails: TS 7 is the native port; it no longer exposes the JS API surface ts-node@10.9.2 reads. `ts.sys` is undefined, so ts-node dies at startup:

    TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fileExists')
    at readConfig (node_modules/ts-node/dist/configuration.js:91:33)

That takes out both `npm test` (test script is `ts-node test/beeatlas-stack.test.ts`) and `cdk synth`/`cdk deploy` (cdk.json app = `npx ts-node bin/infra.ts`). ts-node's latest stable is still 10.9.2 (2023) with only an 11.0.0-beta.1 — so bumping ts-node is not the fix.

Options considered:
- tsx (esbuild-based, drop-in, doesn't touch the typescript JS API) — smallest change: swap the devDependency, cdk.json app, and the test script.
- Node 24 native TS type-stripping — tried it; `node test/beeatlas-stack.test.ts` fails ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on extensionless relative imports (e.g. lib/global-stack). Would require rewriting every import specifier in infra/.

Also worth noting: NO CI workflow builds or tests infra/ (deploy.yml is gone), so PR #55 showed all-green checks while being broken. Verifying infra changes is manual: cd infra && npm run build && npm test && npx cdk synth.

When done, remove the typescript major ignore from the /infra block in .github/dependabot.yml.

title: Ship a page-slug column in occurrences.db so the app can link taxa to /species/ pages
description:
Peter approved linking taxa-pane rows to their /species/ pages (2026-07-26). The app has no way to know which taxa have pages, so links must come from data, not from string manipulation on taxa.name.

CORRECTED ANALYSIS 2026-07-26 (an earlier version of this issue claimed species.json is not authoritative - that was WRONG, and the correction changes the design):

species.json IS the authority. _data/species.js reads it and derives the three lists Eleventy paginates over:
  - species pages: entries with specific_epithet IS NOT NULL, permalink /species/{slug}/
  - genus pages:   ONE PER DISTINCT `genus` FIELD VALUE, not per genus-level slug.
                   This is why /species/Epimelissodes/ returns 200 while no entry
                   carries the slug 'Epimelissodes' - it is a genus value on species rows.
  - subgenus pages: per (genus, subgenus) pair with content.

Checking with the CORRECT rules against the post-synonymy data: of 646 Anthophila taxa with occurrences, only 20 (3%) have no page. The earlier '21 missing' figure was measuring the wrong thing for genera.

Critically, species.json rows carry taxon_id - so a taxon_id -> path map is EXACT, no derivation.

THE 20 WITH NO PAGE (curation backlog, NOT blockers - they simply render as plain text):
Neolarra (genus); Andrena helianthi, Sphecodes ranunculi, Perdita albipennis, Agapostemon angelicus, Atoposmia triodonta, Anthidium maculosum, Epeolus interruptus, Megachile concinna, Anthophora neglecta, Bombus suckleyi, Lasioglossum comagenense, Megachile sublaurita, Triepeolus verbesinae, Lasioglossum gemmatum, Lasioglossum aspilurum, Triepeolus saturninus, Nomada erigeronis, Nomada vegana, Nomada heiligbrodtii.
Peter has said he cannot resolve the synonymy for these, which is exactly why the link must be data-driven: it asks "is there a page" and never "why not".

TWO VIABLE DESIGNS - PICK ONE BEFORE BUILDING

(a) slug column in the taxa table (data/sqlite_export.py).
    The app reads it from occurrences.db, which it already loads - no new fetch.
    COST: sqlite_export must read species.json, which generate-sqlite does NOT
    currently depend on, so it needs a new Stelis edge (species.json -> generate-sqlite).
    That is a CROSS-REPO change and therefore blocked behind beeatlas-cwh's hazard
    (maderas runs whatever stelis is checked out). Also serialises occurrences.db
    behind species-export.

(b) small taxon-pages map emitted by the SITE build.
    _data/species.js already holds the authority, so emitting {taxon_id: path} for
    ~646 taxa (roughly 20 KB, less gzipped) duplicates NO rules. No pipeline change,
    no graph edge, no cross-repo hazard.
    COST: a new runtime artifact plus a fetch on the app path. Note postbuild-data.mjs
    REPLACES _site/data wholesale from the data dir, so this file cannot live in
    _site/data unless it is added to the runtime-artifact list - emit it at a stable
    URL outside _site/data, or enrol it properly in lib/runtime-artifacts.js.

RECOMMENDATION: (b). It keeps the authority in the one place that already computes it, and avoids adding a cross-repo graph edge while cwh is still open.

DO NOT ship derivation-from-name as an interim step: it 404s on real taxa.
acceptance_criteria: Every taxon row that renders a /species/ link resolves to a 200; taxa without a page render as plain text; no link is derived by string manipulation from taxa.name; covered by a test that the linked slug comes from the data, not from the name.
close_reason: Shipped 9b5c600d, via design (b): _data/species.js emits taxonPages (taxon_id -> href) from the three lists Eleventy paginates; published as hashed manifest key taxon_pages by postbuild-data.mjs (dev twin in make-local-manifest.js); fetched lazily when the taxa pane opens. No pipeline change, no Stelis edge, no cross-repo hazard. Verified in-app + live: 25 Bombus rows, 24 linked, Bombus suckleyi plain text; linked hrefs 200, suckleyi 404 (correctly unlinked); family rows unlinked. Degrades to plain text if the map is missing.

title: Surface elevation_dem_m in the app (currently reaches occurrences.db but nothing reads it)
description:
beeatlas-sn8 landed elevation_dem_m in marts/occurrences, so it flows into occurrences.db via sqlite_export's SELECT *. But src/filter.ts OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS is an EXPLICIT select list and does not include it, so the frontend never reads it and the elevation filter still sees only the 45%-populated recorded elevation. The data half of 'Bombus above 1700m' is done; the app half is not.

Measured on the freshly built parquet:
  recorded elevation only ... 12 species from  48 records
  DEM elevation ............. 17 species from 291 records

WHAT THIS NEEDS (and why it is not just 'add a column to the list'):
1. Add 'elevation_dem_m' to OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS + the Occurrence type in src/filter.ts.
2. Decide what the elevation filter means now that there are TWO elevation columns.
   COALESCE(elevation_m, elevation_dem_m) is the obvious rule and is safe to compute
   at the point of use — ADR 0015 deliberately refused to bake it into the pipeline
   so the choice stays visible where it is made.
3. Decide whether the detail card / bee-table distinguish a recorded from a derived
   elevation. ADR 0015's whole premise is that a consumer deserves to know which it
   holds; showing a DEM value unlabelled in the 'Elev (m)' column would undo that.

BLOCKED BY THE SAME OPEN QUESTION AS beeatlas-yc9: yc9 has to settle how a one-sided
elevation bound treats NULLs before this can pick a filter rule, and the two should
be decided together — after DEM backfill the NULL population is checklist-only
(19,929 rows, which must not be backfilled), so the answer may differ from what it
would have been before.
acceptance_criteria: The elevation filter accounts for DEM-derived elevation; a derived elevation is visually distinguishable from a recorded one wherever it is displayed; 'Bombus above 1700m' in the app returns the 17-species answer, not the 12-species one.
close_reason: Shipped 24297056. elevation_dem_m now in OCCURRENCE_COLUMNS -> OccurrenceRow, table column, and CSV (as its own column). Table renders recorded bare / derived with a ~ prefix + header tooltip; precedence mirrors ELEV_SQL. Verified in-app: Bombus elev_min=1500 table page = 100 rows, 16 recorded bare, 84 derived marked, 0 blank (previously all 84 blank). Note: the detail card never displayed elevation, so nothing to change there.

title: One-sided elevation filter does not filter: NULL elevation always passes
acceptance_criteria: Setting only elevMin (or only elevMax) no longer returns the same result set as no elevation filter; the one-sided and two-sided branches of src/filter.ts agree on NULL handling, or the divergence is deliberate and labelled in the UI; 'Bombus above 1700m' does not report 26 species on the strength of 19,156 NULL-elevation records; a regression test covers the one-sided case.
close_reason: Fixed in 1c6bc819. One global rule: COALESCE(elevation_m, elevation_dem_m) compared to the bound; NULLs excluded by SQL semantics in all three bound shapes. Bombus>=1700m goes 26 species/19378 records (== no filter) -> 17 species/299 records. Verified against the live published db. Property-based regressions added. Decision: coalesced+global+NULLs-out, chosen 2026-07-25 after the sn8 backfill made the excluded population checklist-only.

title: Presence artifact + county/ecoregion selector on /species/
description:
Give the static /species/ browse tree county + ecoregion pickers, backed by a small precomputed presence artifact. Second delivery surface for the geography-filtered taxonomy feature; semantics in the parent bead (D-01..D-04).

BLOCKED BY the taxa pane, deliberately: the pane will show which geographies people actually reach for, and this artifact's vocabulary should be chosen with that evidence rather than ahead of it.

WHY AN ARTIFACT, NOT THE DATABASE
/species/ loads no data artifact today — it is a build-time-rendered tree whose only client JS is species-tree.ts. occurrences.db is 32 MB, and pulling it in would change that page's weight budget, the SW precache set, and the offline story. Measured alternative: a county x taxon presence map is 5,614 pairs over 755 taxa = 84 KB raw, 19 KB gzipped. Ecoregions add a comparable second dimension. That is the whole feature for ~1% of the database's cost.

SHAPE
- New build-time artifact, e.g. {county: {taxon_id: [evidence_flags, count]}}, with evidence flags packed so D-01's badges (specimen / community observation / checklist-only) survive into the static page. Follow the existing derived-artifact discipline: data/artifacts.toml provenance, and publication through lib/runtime-artifacts.js + scripts/postbuild-data.mjs (the slim manifest) if it is fetched at runtime rather than inlined by 11ty.
- D-03 applies here for free: county and ecoregion are exactly the granularities at which checklist assertions are legitimate, so the artifact may include them without the placeholder-coordinate problem.
- D-02 does not apply: elevation is not expressible at this granularity and must not be faked. /species/ offers no elevation control.
- Anything richer than county/ecoregion — elevation bands, drawn bounds, named places, year/month/collector — deep-links into the atlas with the filter encoded in the URL. Per D-04 this asymmetry is stated in the UI, not left to be discovered.

VERIFICATION NOTE
_pages/species.njk emits build output asserted by src/tests/build-output.data.test.ts, which npm test does NOT run. Per the npm-test-excludes-the-data-gated-build-output-suite memory, changes here must be verified with npm run test:data — it is the nightly's step-4b hard gate and a green npm test says nothing about it.
design:
STELIS GRAPH (missing from the original write-up). A new published artifact is not just an artifacts.toml + runtime-artifacts.js change — it needs a node in the Stelis graph (~/dev/stelis/src/beeatlas.rkt), which is the sole execution path via npm run fetch-data.

Shape: a 'transform task in the post-dbt siblings section (the block starting around beeatlas.rkt:660, 'NOT upstream of occurrences.db'), modelled on generate-sqlite at :646 —
    (make-task 'taxon-presence-export 'transform
               #:inputs '(occurrences.parquet taxa.csv.gz)
               #:outputs '(taxon_presence.json)
               #:invoke (py "taxon_presence_export" "main"))
plus a (make-artifact 'taxon_presence.json 'file) alongside the declarations at :396-416.

DECLARE EVERY FILE THE INVOCATION WRITES. species-export (:688) carries a scar comment about exactly this: its slice-1 edge declared 2 of the 6 files it actually writes, and edge-verify (stelis st-qp7) caught the other four as undeclared writes. If this export emits a sibling feed, declare it.

Reads occurrences.parquet, not occurrences.db — the parquet mart is what post-dbt exports consume (st-4cm placed-marts, beeatlas.rkt:655).
acceptance_criteria: /species/ gains county + ecoregion pickers and still loads no SQL engine and no occurrences.db; the presence artifact stays under ~25 KB gzipped and carries evidence flags so D-01 badges survive; checklist assertions are included (county/ecoregion is their legitimate granularity, D-03); no elevation control is offered (D-02); richer queries deep-link into the atlas with the filter encoded, and the UI says so (D-04); verified with npm run test:data, not just npm test.
close_reason: Shipped: beeatlas 32cfe7ac + stelis 20538b0. taxon_presence.json (8060 pairs, 15.7 KB gzipped, under the 25 KB budget) with evidence bitmasks; county+ecoregion pickers on /species/; no SQL engine, no occurrences.db. D-03 checklist included (legitimate granularity), D-02 no elevation control, D-04 asymmetry stated in the UI with a deep link into the atlas. Verified with npm run test:data (1074 pass), not just npm test. In-page: 591 -> 156 species for King County, 246 for North Cascades, composes with the text filter, restores on clear. Dropped per-place counts deliberately (10 KB gzipped, would break budget); statewide counts are hidden while filtered rather than shown misleadingly.

title: Taxa pane: taxonomic tree of the current filter's result set
description:
Add a taxonomic-tree view of the CURRENT filter's result set to the map app, as a third paneState beside 'list' and 'table'. This is the first delivery surface for the geography-filtered taxonomy feature; semantics are defined in the parent bead (D-01..D-04) and are not restated here except where they bind implementation.

WHY THE PANE FIRST: the app already owns every geographic filter this needs (selectedCounties, selectedEcoregions, selectedPlace, bounds, elevMin/elevMax — src/filter.ts:14-28). No new filter vocabulary, no new data artifact, and it composes with year/month/collector/tier filters for free. The static /species/ half is the follow-up.

SHAPE
- url-state.ts:351 currently parses paneState as 'list' | 'table' | 'collapsed'. Add 'taxa' to the union, the parser, and the serializer (url-state.ts:113) so /?counties=King&pane=taxa is shareable exactly as pane=list is today. Legacy view=table aliasing is untouched.
- bee-pane.ts:55 declares the same union as a @property — update both; they are two independent literals of one vocabulary.
- Query: aggregate the filtered occurrence set by taxon_id, joined to the taxa table for rank/lineage, rather than materializing rows. Reuse the buildWhere machinery in filter.ts so the pane can never drift from what the map is showing.
- Render with the species-tree.ts rank model (rank-skipped for subfamily/tribe/subgenus, "Show all ranks" toggle). Respect its CR-01 invariant: never use the hidden attribute to skip a rank — that buries the subtree.

BINDING SEMANTICS (from the parent)
- D-02: when elevMin/elevMax is set, this pane adds elevation_m IS NOT NULL. Other panes keep filter.ts's permissive behavior, so the SAME filter yields different membership in different panes. This must be visible in the pane — a line stating how many taxa are excluded for lack of elevation data, with an escape hatch to show them.
- D-03: when bounds or selectedPlace is active, exclude record_type='checklist'. County/ecoregion filters keep it.
- D-01: badge each taxon with its evidence in this geography (specimen / community observation / checklist-only).

CONSTRAINT THAT BITES
Adding a filter dimension is a REQUIRED-field change across every FilterState literal — see the project_filterstate_required_field_contract memory. This bead adds no FilterState field (elevation NULL handling is a clause change inside buildWhere, and paneState lives in UiState, not FilterState), so that trap should not fire. Verify with tsc rather than assuming.

OPEN
Whether the pane's per-taxon row links to /species/<slug>/ (leaves the app) or selects that taxon in the current filter (stays in the app). Both are defensible; decide during build with the map open.
acceptance_criteria: pane=taxa parses and serializes in url-state.ts and is shareable like pane=list; the tree is built from the same buildWhere output the map uses, so it cannot disagree with the map; the pane's elevation handling is filter.ts's ELEV_SQL (no pane-specific rule — D-02's divergence was superseded by yc9, see notes); when an elevation bound is active the pane discloses that taxa attested only by county-level checklist records are excluded, and how many; bounds/place filters exclude record_type='checklist' while county/ecoregion filters retain it; each taxon badges specimen / community-observation / checklist-only evidence; 'Megachilidae genera in King County' and 'Bombus species above 1700m' both return evidence-backed answers (the latter = 17 species); tsc clean and npm test green.
notes:
SHIPPED 2026-07-26 in 8701c08e (pane), building on 1c6bc819 (yc9) and d044677f (sn8).

DELIVERED: pane=taxa as a third paneState, shareable/round-tripping in url-state; aggregate via the same buildFilterSQL the map uses; species-tree.ts rank model reused (same data-rank/data-name contract + shared localStorage toggle key); D-01 evidence badges with ancestor roll-up; D-03 checklist exclusion for bounds/place; D-02's disclosure (per the superseded-D-02 note above).

VERIFIED IN THE APP against real published data:
  - Bombus >=1700m: 17 species + 'so 3 taxa are not shown' disclosure
  - Megachilidae in King County: 10 genera, Stelis badged checklist-only
  - rank toggle: 14 intermediate ranks revealed, all 40 species still rendered (CR-01)
  - bbox around the downtown Seattle placeholder: 18 species, ZERO checklist evidence (D-03)

TWO BUGS FOUND BY RUNNING IT (both fixed in the same commit):
  1. _resolveLegacyTaxon re-ran only _runFilterQuery, so a legacy ?taxon=<name> deep
     link left panes showing pre-resolution unfiltered results. A RACE (taxaReady vs
     loadOccurrencesTable) that the table pane happened to win locally — latent for
     list/table too, not just the new pane.
  2. paneState='taxa' matched no .content class, so bee-pane got no positioning.

STILL OPEN (was already flagged OPEN in the description): the per-taxon row currently
SELECTS the taxon in the current filter (stays in the app, preserves geography). It does
NOT link to /species/<slug>/. Both were defensible; in-app selection won because the pane
exists to explore THIS result set and leaving would discard the geography filter. If a
species-page link is wanted too, it needs a second affordance per row — that is a UI
pattern question, not a code question.

NOT ADDRESSED: non-bee families appear in the tree when the filter admits them (e.g.
Bombyliidae, Lestica) — they are in the occurrence data and every other pane shows them
too, so this is pre-existing, not a pane defect. Filed separately if it matters.
close_reason: Shipped 8701c08e; verified in-app against real data. See notes for the two bugs found by UAT and the one deliberately-left-open UI question.

title: Fetch the expert iNat feed from the API instead of a committed CSV
description:
ARM 4 (record_type='inat_expert') is the only occurrence arm whose upstream is a hand-refreshed file. data/inat_obs_pipeline.py reads data/raw/inat_expert_obs.csv (8.9 MB, committed), which is produced by replaying a browser request recorded in data/raw/inat_expert_obs.sh. Every other source — inaturalist, waba, projects, ecdysis — is a live loader. Make this one match.

WHY NOW: the snapshot is from 2026-05-26 and is already 1,553 observations short. Same query, same 11-name roster, run against the API on 2026-07-25: 31,265 results vs 29,712 rows in the CSV (~5% drift in two months). The 8 identifiers added on 2026-07-25 (+372 observations) are inert until someone re-runs the export by hand. A live loader removes the manual step and the drift.

TARGET SHAPE — copy data/inaturalist_pipeline.py: dlt rest_api_resources against api.inaturalist.org/v2, primary_key uuid, write_disposition merge, per_page=200, explicit fields=, processing_steps map for geojson->lat/lon. Verified 2026-07-25 that v2 accepts ident_user_id (56,455 filtered vs 86,131 unfiltered for place_id=46&taxon_id=630955).

CONSTRAINT THAT BITES — do NOT reuse the page_number paginator. iNat caps the pagination window at 10,000 rows; page=51&per_page=200 returns HTTP 500, and this result set is ~31.6k. Use id_above cursor pagination (order_by=id&order=asc&id_above=N), verified working on v2. Note this is a latent risk in inaturalist_pipeline.py too if that project ever crosses 10k on a full reload — out of scope here, worth a separate look.

THE ROSTER: currently the EXPERTS array in data/raw/inat_expert_obs.sh. Move it to a real config surface (config.toml [sources.inat_obs] or config.py) so the loader is its single definition. Keep the caveat comment with it: ident_user_id filters on who *identified* an observation, not who observed it, and not agreement with the community taxon we ingest. See docs/domain-model.md Category 4.

QUERY TO PRESERVE (from the .sh): quality_grade=any, identifications=any, geoprivacy=open, taxon_geoprivacy=open, place_id=46 (Washington), taxon_id=630955 (Anthophila), hrank=genus, acc_below_or_unknown=100, ident_user_id=<roster>.

FIELD MAPPING to settle: the CSV's 'field:associated species with names lookup' becomes an ofvs entry (resolve its field_id, as waba_pipeline.py does for 18116); license -> license_code; image_url -> photos (CSV gives one URL, API gives a photo list — pick a rule); obs_url stays constructed from the id.

DEDUP: _load_excluded_ids currently drops obs already represented as Ecdysis specimens by reading dbt_sandbox.int_waba_link at load time — a dbt dependency inside a boundary loader. Decide whether that survives as a post-load step or moves downstream into int_combined, which already has the CR-01 exclusion.

FREE FIX: resolves beeatlas-rzb — quality_grade is always NULL today because the export form never selected the column. The API returns it.

STELIS: no graph change needed. 'inat-obs is already a boundary task with #:outputs '(inat_obs_data) (stelis src/beeatlas.rkt:565), and the existing 'inat-obs-integrity count-swing gate is exactly the safety net a newly-live source wants.

CLEANUP once a live run matches the snapshot within the gate's tolerance: delete data/raw/inat_expert_obs.csv and data/raw/inat_expert_obs.sh, and update docs/domain-model.md Category 4 (which currently points at the .sh as the roster's home).
acceptance_criteria:
- inat_obs_data.observations is populated by an API loader with no committed CSV in the path
- Loader pages past 10k rows without a 500 (id_above cursor, verified on a full reload)
- Roster lives in config, not in a shell script; adding a login needs no hand-run export
- quality_grade is non-NULL for inat_expert rows (closes beeatlas-rzb)
- Row count is within the inat-obs-integrity gate's tolerance of the 29,712-row snapshot on first live run

title: Filter species list by geography
description:
I would like to list e.g. all the genera of Megachilidae present in King County, or all the species of Bombus present above 1700m elevation.

This bead holds the SEMANTICS that both delivery surfaces share; the work itself is in the two children. Grilled 2026-07-25 — the decisions below are settled, not proposals.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (don't rebuild it)
- The map app's FilterState (src/filter.ts:14-28) already carries selectedCounties, selectedEcoregions, elevMin/elevMax, selectedPlace and bounds. Geographic filtering of OCCURRENCES is done. What is missing is a taxon-shaped VIEW of that result set.
- Place detail pages already render "Bees found here" as species-by-genus (_pages/place-detail.njk:52-73), built by data/places_export.py.
- /species/ (_pages/species.njk) is a fully build-time-rendered tree whose only client behavior is a text filter + rank toggle (src/species-tree.ts). It loads no data artifact.

THE DATA (public/data/occurrences.db, 32 MB; tables occurrences, occurrence_places, taxa, geo_blob)
98,775 rows / 39 counties, by record_type: specimen 49,919 · inat_expert 28,850 · checklist 19,929 · waba_specimen 40 · provisional_sample 37.

D-01 PRESENCE = THE CURRENT FILTER'S RESULT SET.
No new filter vocabulary. hiddenTiers governs inclusion exactly as it does for the map. Each taxon carries a badge showing what backs it IN THAT GEOGRAPHY: specimen-backed / community-observed / checklist-only. This surfaces the atlas-vs-other tier distinction at the taxon level, which the map already encodes as symbology. Rejected: "atlas records only" — it would answer "no Megachile pugnata in King County" when the published checklist says otherwise.

D-02 ELEVATION DEMANDS POSITIVE EVIDENCE.
In a taxon view, any elevation bound implies elevation_m IS NOT NULL. Map/list/table panes keep today's permissive behavior — "don't hide points we can't place" is defensible for plotting, not for a presence claim. The divergence MUST be visible in the UI, not merely documented.
Why: elevation_m is populated on 44,218 of 98,775 rows (45%) and comes ONLY from the Ecdysis arm — int_combined.sql hardcodes NULL::INTEGER for the other four arms (lines 115, 167, 255, 319). Measured against the bead's own example, "Bombus above 1700m" today returns 26 species, which is identical to applying no elevation filter at all; the evidence-backed answer is 12 species from 48 records, while 19,156 records pass purely because their elevation is NULL. See the filter.ts bug bead for the underlying defect.

D-03 CHECKLIST ASSERTIONS COUNT AT COUNTY/ECOREGION GRANULARITY ONLY.
County and ecoregion filters include checklist rows (their county is authoritative — Bartholomew et al. 2024 county-range assertions). Bounds and named-place filters EXCLUDE them, because below county their coordinate is a placeholder: 6,090 of 19,929 checklist rows (31%) sit on just 45 shared points, e.g. 683 King County rows parked on one coordinate in downtown Seattle. 1,989 checklist rows already fall inside named-place polygons via occurrence_places.
Precedent: data/places_export.py:145 already filters occ.tier = 'atlas' for the place-scoped species list, so place pages are unaffected by this and need no change.

D-04 TWO SURFACES, TWO GEOGRAPHY VOCABULARIES — DELIBERATELY.
The taxa pane gets the full expressive filter (counties, ecoregions, places, drawn bounds, elevation, and for free: year, month, collector, tier). /species/ gets county + ecoregion only, backed by a small precomputed artifact so it stays a static page. Anything richer deep-links from /species/ into the atlas carrying the filter. This asymmetry is a product statement and must be stated in the UI, not left to be discovered.

SHARED PRESENTATION
- Per-taxon count = filtered record count. Collapsed parents show child-taxon counts ("31 spp.").
- Reuse species-tree.ts's rank model (intermediate subfamily/tribe/subgenus collapsed via rank-skipped, "Show all ranks" toggle) rather than inventing a second tree behavior. Note its CR-01 invariant: never use the hidden attribute to skip a rank.

CHILDREN
1. Taxa pane in the map app.
2. Presence artifact + /species/ geography selector (blocked by 1).
RELATED: the filter.ts elevation-NULL bug (independent — it misleads the shipped map today), and DEM elevation backfill (would raise elevation coverage from 45% to ~89% and make D-02 far less lossy).
acceptance_criteria: Semantics D-01..D-04 are settled and both children reference them rather than re-deciding. This bead closes when both children close; it ships no code itself.
notes:
D-02 SUPERSEDED 2026-07-25. Its premise — elevation_m populated on only 45% of rows, from the Ecdysis arm alone — was removed by beeatlas-sn8 (DEM backfill: elevation_dem_m, 100% coverage on all four non-checklist arms) and beeatlas-yc9 (the filter now applies ONE global rule, COALESCE(elevation_m, elevation_dem_m) with NULLs excluded, in every pane).

So there is no 'taxon view demands positive evidence while map/list/table stay permissive' asymmetry to build: every surface demands positive evidence now. D-02's real content survives as a DISCLOSURE requirement on the child bead, and it is sharper than originally framed — the excluded set is exactly the 124 taxa attested only by county-level checklist records, not a diffuse 'missing data' population.

D-01, D-03, D-04 are unaffected.

title: Ecdysis loader: cheap v2-API change-probe to skip unchanged re-ingests
description:
load_ecdysis pays a ~2-minute server-side ZIP build every run; past the 6h mtime TTL (the nightly) it downloaded unconditionally. The Symbiota download UI exposes no high-water-mark, but Ecdysis's v2 REST API does.

MECHANISM (in data/ecdysis_pipeline.py):
- Probe GET https://ecdysis.org/api/v2/occurrence UNAUTHENTICATED, scoped by datasetID=44 — the ZIP's exact population. Dataset 44 is a 46,090-record subset of WSUC collection 164 (=106,870), so datasetID (NOT collid) is the correct scope.
- Two complementary signals vs a baseline recorded at last download:
  * total count           -> catches deletions / net membership changes
  * modified-since count   -> catches adds+edits (omoccurrences.dateLastModified; populated on 100% of ds-44 records, so no NULL-on-insert leak). Baseline is the modified-since count AT DOWNLOAD TIME (not zero); 'changed' = grew past baseline. 'since' backed off one day for TZ safety.
- Reuse cached ZIP iff BOTH signals match baseline. Conservative: no baseline / probe error / either moved => download. Gated by ECDYSIS_SKIP_PROBE (=0 reverts).

DECISION: nightly may skip. Residual gap = same-interval compensating replace (N deleted + N inserted, total flat) with back-dated inserts — rare, self-heals on the next full pull.

UPSTREAM BUG (verified live 2026-07-23): v2 API dateLastModifiedMin WITHOUT a Max returns HTTP 500 (loose whereRaw binding, OccurrenceController.php:461). Workaround: always pass a far-future Max. Also: dwcapubhandler's IFNULL(modified,datelastmodified) filter is STALER than the API's dateLastModified, so the v2 API is the correct source.

STATUS: prototype landed (_api_occurrence_count / _record_probe_baseline / _probe_says_unchanged + _download_zip wiring). Smoke-tested against the live API in the 3.14 runtime; NOT yet exercised through a full dlt load (needs maderas-only creds). Stelis side (surface the skip in --why/--explain, H2) tracked separately in the stelis repo.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-07-31. The two outstanding items are done.

1. VERIFIED IN PRODUCTION (the "not yet exercised through a full dlt load" gap).
   The nightly of 2026-07-31 03:00 on maderas took the skip path for real:
     ▶ ecdysis
       Ecdysis source unchanged since last pull (change-probe); reusing cached ZIP
       Pipeline ecdysis load step completed in 58.01 seconds
       Load package 1785534628.8482463 is LOADED and contains no failed jobs
     ✓ ecdysis — exit 0
       ≡ outputs identical to last build — early cutoff
   So the reused ZIP feeds dlt correctly and Stelis's content-addressing agrees the
   outputs are unchanged. Live sidecar: {"dataset_id":44,"since":"2026-07-30",
   "total":46090,"baseline_changed":4}. No hand-run needed; maderas creds not needed.

2. TEST COVERAGE ADDED (145ee1ae) — data/tests/test_ecdysis_probe.py, 18 fast-tier
   tests grouped by the property they protect: cheapness (unchanged => 2 GETs, 0 POSTs;
   in-TTL => 0 GETs), conservatism (no sidecar / either signal moved / probe error /
   corrupt sidecar / corrupt cache / SKIP_PROBE=0 all download), baseline truth, and
   the far-future-Max HTTP-500 workaround. Mutation-checked: removing the
   _is_valid_cached_zip guard, the total comparison, the far-future Max, or flipping
   the error return to True each fails at least one test.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED in the same commit:

a. Baseline was read AFTER the download. A record inserted during the ~2-minute ZIP
   build may or may not be in the ZIP, but was folded into the baseline either way, so
   the probe hid it until an unrelated edit tripped a signal. Now read BEFORE the POST
   (_read_probe_baseline) and written only on success (_write_probe_baseline), so the
   worst case is a redundant download rather than a hidden record. The split also stops
   a FAILED download — which returns the OLD cached ZIP — from stamping a baseline
   describing a source state that cache never caught up to; that would have licensed
   skipping indefinitely. This is a third blind spot beyond the two already documented,
   and unlike those two it did NOT self-heal on the next pull.

b. Fast-tier network leak: test_ecdysis_auth.py patched only requests.Session, but the
   probe reads the v2 API via module-level requests.get — so every success-path auth
   test was making two live calls to ecdysis.org. Stubbed at the seam.

STILL OPEN ELSEWHERE: the Stelis-side --why/--explain surfacing (H2) remains tracked in
the stelis repo, not here.

title: Decide: is a popover the right surface for the account menu at compact widths?
description:
Apple HIG (Popovers, verified by direct browser fetch 2026-07-18) states: 'Avoid displaying popovers in compact views. Reserve popovers for wide views; for compact views, use all available screen space by presenting information in a full-screen modal view like a sheet instead.'

BeeAtlas's account/status menu is a popover, and the widths that motivated the whole pattern-library effort (<=640px, 320-390px especially) are compact views. If Apple is right for this case, the surface itself is wrong at mobile widths and no amount of internal hierarchy tuning fixes it — which would reframe beeatlas-0lk from 'restyle the menu' to 'the menu becomes a sheet below the breakpoint'.

Arguments to weigh: (a) the guidance is written for iOS/iPadOS NATIVE apps; BeeAtlas is a web app (its PWA install target is iOS Safari, so the audience overlaps but the platform contract does not); (b) no equivalent compact-width rule was found in Material or the web design systems surveyed — though Material's pages were unreachable, so that is an unverified absence, not a contradiction; (c) a sheet dissolves the close-button question, since sheets carry a dismiss affordance by convention; (d) a responsive surface (popover >=641px, sheet below) doubles the shell's states and its test matrix.

See section 11.1a of docs/product/research/menu-patterns-mixed-content.md.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded (with rationale) on whether the compact-width menu stays a popover, becomes a sheet, or the shell goes responsive — before beeatlas-0lk restyles anything.

title: Apply the pattern library + tokens to the header account menu
description: The concrete payoff for beeatlas-2lb: restyle the account/status menu built in beeatlas-j96 so its five content kinds read as a clear hierarchy. Known specific problems: full-width bordered accent buttons (.cache-popover__update-btn, reused for Sign in / Sign out / update-available) are the loudest thing in a mostly-passive menu; the 'Source code' link row and the status rows share a treatment despite one being interactive; four type/color treatments compete in a 240-320px surface.
design: DECIDED 2026-07-18 (user): no borders on in-menu action buttons — the bordered accent treatment (.cache-popover__update-btn, currently reused for Sign in / Sign out / update-available) is dropped in favor of plain full-bleed rows with a hover/press background state layer, per research section 5. Consequence: .cache-popover__update-btn stops being the shared action treatment; the update-available notice keeps emphasis via an accent-tinted row BACKGROUND, not an outline. UNDER RESEARCH: whether the shell keeps its X dismiss button and header row at all (see research section 11 when it lands) — this may remove .cache-popover__header, which all three popovers currently share.
acceptance_criteria: The menu uses only the documented row types and tokens; a status line is visually distinguishable from a link at a glance.
notes:
CLOSE BUTTON (research section 11): remove the X from the account/status menu — the trigger stays visible and toggles, so it IS the close control (Radix DropdownMenu ships no Close part; Radix Popover does, and 'adheres to the Dialog WAI-ARIA pattern'). No spec requires it: the APG close-button line is 'strongly recommended' and written for MODAL dialogs where the trigger is inert; no WCAG SC requires a visible close on click-triggered non-modal content (1.4.13 covers hover/focus triggers only). Removing it also collapses the header row, letting the account identity become a pure non-interactive header block — one fewer competing element in the region flagged as irregular. Shell gains dismissible:boolean + heading?:string; A2HS passes both, account menu neither.

CAVEAT on the A2HS half: Apple's 'Use a Close button for confirmation and guidance only' is VERIFIED verbatim, but its own gloss is 'like exiting with or without saving changes' — confirmation-flavored, about unsaved work. Reading 'guidance' to cover the A2HS how-to is plausible but not clearly Apple's intent; that recommendation rests mainly on the reasoned cost-of-accidental-dismissal argument, which is an inference.

title: UI pattern library: reusable patterns, design tokens, and a proofing page
description:
The header account menu (beeatlas-j96) exposed the underlying gap: BeeAtlas has no shared vocabulary for UI surfaces. That menu now stacks five content kinds — an identity row with a role badge, full-width bordered action buttons, passive status lines, a navigation link, and small meta text — each with its own visual treatment, producing (user's words) 'too much visual irregularity and unclear information hierarchy'. Components are Lit elements with shadow DOM, so styles cannot leak between them and every surface has re-invented its own spacing, type scale and row treatments by copy-paste (the .cache-popover shell has been cloned three times: cache, iOS A2HS, account).

Compounding this: code comments in src/bee-header.ts (x2), src/bee-atlas.ts and src/prime-orchestrator.ts (x3) cite 'PATTERNS.md' as the authority for these shells — but PATTERNS.md was DELETED in commit f1ba04f0 (the GSD->beads migration). The pattern authority the code points at does not exist. This epic should produce its successor.

Scope: (1) design tokens for shared UI internals, (2) a written pattern library documenting the reusable surfaces, (3) a proofing page rendering each element across its states so regressions and irregularity are visible at a glance.
design: Shadow DOM means tokens must be CSS custom properties inherited from the document root (or an adopted stylesheet) — per-component css`` blocks cannot share values otherwise. Existing root tokens live in src/index.css (--header-bg, --accent, --border, --text-body, --text-hint). Research grounding: docs/product/research/menu-patterns-mixed-content.md.

title: Reconcile Bombus californicus/fervidus synonymy against iNat's Bombus fervidus complex
description:
BeeAtlas treats Bombus californicus as a JUNIOR SYNONYM of Bombus fervidus. iNaturalist does not: it keeps both as separate taxa nested inside a 'Bombus fervidus complex'. We need to decide how our taxonomy maps onto theirs wherever we query or join against iNat taxon IDs.

This is a general instance of a problem we will keep hitting: our synonymy decisions and iNat's taxon graph disagree, and any place we resolve a canonical_name to a single iNat taxon_id silently picks one side.

Known consequences to check:
- Photo seeding (scripts/seed-species-photos.mjs) resolves one taxon_id per scientificName via the canonical_to_taxon_id bridge. If we resolve to iNat's narrow B. fervidus, every WA observation identified as B. californicus is invisible to the query — plausibly why the fervidus photo search fell back out of region despite plenty of WA fervidus records. Under our synonymy we should be querying BOTH taxa (or the complex).
- The occurrence arms that join on iNat taxon identity may be split the same way.
- Checklist synonymy: per feedback_checklist_synonymy_gap, a synonym applied in int_combined but not stg_checklist__species creates a ghost zero-occurrence row. Verify which side californicus is handled on.

Needs a decision recorded in docs/adr/ once resolved (per CLAUDE.md: add an ADR when a decision is made).
design:
Questions to settle:
- Do we keep californicus as a junior synonym of fervidus, or follow iNat and split? Whose treatment is current in the literature?
- Where a single iNat taxon_id is required, do we map a BeeAtlas species to a SET of iNat taxon IDs instead of a scalar?
- Does the 'complex' taxon itself have a usable taxon_id we can query to capture both children at once?
- Are there other BeeAtlas synonymies with the same shape? Audit rather than fix only this one.
acceptance_criteria: Treatment decided and recorded in an ADR; taxon-id resolution handles the fervidus/californicus case correctly wherever iNat taxon IDs are used; audit done for other affected synonymies.
notes: Raised by Peter 2026-07-18 alongside beeatlas-zd7 (photo selection). Peter flagged this explicitly as 'a separate issue to think through' — do not fold it into the photo work, but note it may be a prerequisite for correct WA photo selection.

title: Improve species photo selection criteria and re-select photos for all species
description:
The curated hero photos in content/species-photos.toml were seeded by scripts/seed-species-photos.mjs using selection criteria that optimize for the wrong thing. Re-select photos for every species under better criteria.

Observed failure (Bombus fervidus): all three photos on the species page come from a single iNat observation (56979330, Brandie Dunn, Johnsburg IL). It was chosen because it has many faves — but it has many faves precisely because it is an UNUSUAL individual, which makes it a poor reference image. It is also out of region despite plenty of WA fervidus observations existing.

Three distinct defects in the current seeder:

1. order_by=votes (scripts/seed-species-photos.mjs:172) ranks by iNat faves. Faves reward striking/aberrant/charismatic individuals — a selection pressure directly AGAINST the typical, diagnostic individual a reference photo needs.

2. extractPhotos (scripts/seed-species-photos.mjs:57-78) loops photos WITHIN an observation before advancing to the next observation, so one observation with 3+ license-clean photos consumes the entire quota. That is exactly what happened for fervidus. Photos should be diversified across distinct observations.

3. Region preference is too weak. fetchPhotosForTaxon (scripts/seed-species-photos.mjs:191-202) tries WA (place_id=46) then tops up GLOBALLY with no intermediate PNW tier and no floor on how far afield it will reach.
design:
Direction (to be refined):
- Prefer Washington, then PNW (OR/ID/BC), then wider — add an intermediate regional tier instead of WA-then-global.
- Strongly prefer photos from SPECIMEN observations (records tied to our specimen arm / vouchered material), which are far more likely to show a determinable, typical individual than a charismatic in-situ shot.
- Replace or supplement order_by=votes with a criterion that does not reward aberrance.

title: Non-deterministic build outputs: topology built_at timestamp + collectors-events row order
description:
Two post-dbt export steps produce byte-nondeterministic output — rebuilding the same snapshot yields different bytes, violating the determinism property a content-addressed build (stelis) depends on. Surfaced by stelis's --run-vs-direct parity check while authoring these as graph terminals (stelis st-4cm slice 4). In both cases the underlying geometry/data is deterministic; only an incidental field varies.

SITE 1 — topology_postprocess.py: _inject_meta stamps _meta.built_at with a wall-clock UTC timestamp (e.g. 2026-07-12T22:19:54Z). Every run of counties/ecoregions/wilderness.clean.geojson differs solely in that field (geometry byte-identical after stripping _meta, confirmed). Fix: derive the stamp from something content-stable (git_sha is already stamped and sufficient; or the source commit's author date; or honor SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH) rather than time.time().

SITE 2 — collectors_events_export.py: the first_page_events array for a collector can come back in a DIFFERENT ORDER across runs — same 100 events, identical as a multiset, reordered (observed on 1 of 124 collectors). The event query's ORDER BY isn't a total order, so tied rows are ordered by DuckDB's parallel scan nondeterministically. Same root cause likely affects collector_event_pages.json (also differs run-to-run). Fix: add a deterministic tiebreak to the ORDER BY (e.g. append occurrence id / a unique key) so tied rows have a stable order.

WHY IT MATTERS: DESIGN 'Determinism is a day-one property — build the same snapshot twice, compare hashes.' Non-deterministic outputs mean stelis's cache never gets early cutoff on these targets (every rebuild reads as changed) and --verify fails for them. The single-file exports (species/collectors/places.json) carry neither a timestamp nor an unordered array, which is why they were byte-stable in slices 2/3.
notes: SITE 1 CONTRACT (stelis ADR 0004 / st-3mi now landed on the stelis side): stelis injects SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (= beeatlas HEAD committer date, e.g. $(git log -1 --format=%ct)) into every task's hermetic env. FIX for topology_postprocess._inject_meta: read SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from os.environ and use it as built_at (format the int epoch as ISO8601 UTC, e.g. datetime.fromtimestamp(int(sde), tz=timezone.utc)); fall back to time.time() ONLY when the var is unset, so the script stays runnable standalone (nightly) but is byte-deterministic under stelis. Verified on the stelis side: the epoch reaches the subprocess env end-to-end, is numeric + stable across calls. Once topology reads it, stelis 'racket src/main.rkt --verify counties.clean.geojson' becomes a real determinism gate (geometry was already stable). SITE 2 already fixed (0a025ff4).
close_reason: Both sites fixed and verified from stelis. title: Eliminate in-place mutation of sibling-task outputs (clean read-modify-write)
description:
Two build steps mutate a file that a DIFFERENT step already produced, instead of writing a fresh, distinctly-named artifact. This breaks one-producer-per-artifact, which is what a content-addressed build graph (stelis st-4cm) needs to model these steps as nodes. Make each step write its own distinct output.

SITE 1 — topology_postprocess.py: reads counties/ecoregions/wilderness.geojson from EXPORT_DIR (the dbt-mart copies place-marts drops there) and rewrites them IN PLACE via mapshaper -clean/-simplify (write-to-sibling-tmp then rename over original). Input path == output path. Clean shape: read the raw mart copy, write a distinctly-named cleaned file (e.g. <name>.clean.geojson or a cleaned/ subdir), and point downstream consumers (the frontend map layers) at the cleaned name.

SITE 2 — collectors_events_export.py: reads collectors.json (produced by collectors_export.py), appends event fields (first_page_events, total_event_pages, total_event_count) to each record, and writes collectors.json BACK — overwriting a sibling step's output. Also writes collector_event_pages.json (that one is already a distinct output and is fine). Clean shape: write the enriched result to a distinct name (e.g. collectors.events.json) that the frontend loads, leaving collectors.json owned solely by collectors-export; or restructure so the base is an intermediate and collectors-events-export is the sole producer of the final collectors.json.

WHY NOW: stelis needs to author these as graph terminals. As long as they mutate a sibling's file, stelis would have to model a two-producers-per-artifact / read-modify-write shape (undesirable). Cleaning beeatlas collapses shape #2 into the ordinary single-file (and directory) shapes stelis already handles.

Frontend + deploy consumers of the renamed files must be updated in the same change.
notes: Filed from stelis st-4cm modeling. Both sites confirmed by reading the scripts: topology_postprocess.py main() loops EXPORT_DIR/*.geojson and _run_mapshaper overwrites in place; collectors_events_export.py export_collector_events() reads collectors.json and writes out_path=ASSETS_DIR/collectors.json. run.py step ordering (collectors-export -> collectors-events-export -> notes-harvest) currently relies on the in-place mutation being visible to later steps (notes-harvest reads collectors.json for byline resolution) — renaming means notes-harvest must read whichever file now carries display_name.
close_reason: Both sites cleaned. topology_postprocess.py reads raw <name>.geojson read-only and writes distinct <name>.clean.geojson (dbt-build owns the raw mart, this step owns .clean). collectors_events_export.py reads base collectors.json read-only and writes distinct collectors.events.json + collector_event_pages.json; base collectors.json owned solely by collectors-export. Verified by reading the scripts. Downstream (manifest 'collectors' key -> collectors.events.json; notes-harvest still reads base collectors.json for display_name, which enrichment never touched).

design:

Spine = PULL-discovery (self-serve) first; PUSH (targeted invitations, ask-a-question, trip reports) is a fast-follow because each has a cold-start dependency. Central opportunity = anaemic place pages (today: name + count + owner + atlas link only) -> per-place temporal collecting intelligence.

DOMAIN (now in CONTEXT.md): 'target host' (prospective plant to seek; sources = curated project lists + WA-endemic natives via WNPS + specialist-bee hosts from bee_specialist_hosts.csv) vs 'sample host' (retrospective, a.k.a. floral host). inat_host/species_host are columns, NOT concepts.
